translations.text: The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah son of Hilkiah, one of the priests, who lived in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
The word of God came to him in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, in the thirteenth year of his reign.
It also came in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, until the eleventh year of Zedekiah, king of Judah, until Jerusalem was taken captive in the fifth month.
And the word of the Lord came to him:
"Before you were formed in your mother's womb I knew you, and before you came out of the womb I made you holy. I appointed you as a prophet over the nations and peoples."
And I said, "O Lord, you who are, look, I do not know how to speak, for I am only a youth."
And the Lord said to me, "Do not say, 'I am only a youth,' for you shall go to everyone I send you to, and you shall speak everything I command you.
Do not be afraid of them, and do not be terrified in front of them, for I am with you to rescue you, says the Lord."
And the Lord stretched out his hand to me and touched my mouth, and the Lord said to me, "Look, I have put my words in your mouth.
Look, today I have set you over nations and kingdoms, to uproot and to dig up, to destroy and to tear down, to build and to plant."
And the word of the Lord came to me, and he said to me, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" And I said, "I see a rod of a nut tree."
And the Lord said to me, "You have seen well, for I am watching over my words to carry them out."
And the word of the Lord came to me a second time, and he said, "What do you see?" And I said, "I see a [?] (a cauldron?) heated from beneath, and it is facing away from the north."
And the Lord said to me, "From the north disaster will break out on all who live in the land.

For look, I will call all the kings of the kingdoms from the land of the north, says the Lord, and they will come, and each of them will set up his throne at the thresholds of the gates of Jerusalem, and against all its surrounding walls, and against all the cities of Judah.
And I will pronounce my judgment on them for all their wickedness, because they abandoned me, and sacrificed to foreign gods, and worshipped what their own hands had made.

And you, prepare yourself for action. Get up and tell them everything I command you. Do not be afraid of them, and do not tremble in front of them, for I am with you to make you strong, says the Lord.
And look, today I have made you like a fortified city, like an iron pillar, and like a bronze wall against all the kings of Judah, and its princes, and their priests, and the people of the land.
They will fight against you, but they will not defeat you, for I am with you to rescue you, says the Lord."
And the word of the Lord came to me, and he said, "Go and read this aloud so that the people of Israel hear it. Answer them and say,
'This is what the Lord says: I have remembered with mercy your youth, and the love of your completion, when you followed the Holy One of Israel, says the Lord, in the wilderness, in a land not sown.'
Israel is holy to the Lord, the first of his harvest. Everyone who devours him will regret it.
Hear the word of the Lord, house of Jacob, and all the tribes of the house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord: What fault did your fathers find in me, that they went far away from me, and followed after the track of vain things, and became vain themselves,

and they did not say: "Where is the Lord, who brought us out of the land of Egypt, who led us through the wilderness, through a strange and pathless land, a land without water and without fruit, and the shadow of death, a land through which no man passed, nor did any son of man dwell there"?
And I brought you into Carmel to eat its good fruits. But you entered and defiled my land, and made my inheritance an abomination.

The priests did not say, "Where is the Lord?" Those learned in the law did not know me. The shepherds acted ungodly toward me. The prophets prophesied by Baal and followed after an unprofitable track.
Therefore I will again bring judgment against you, says the Lord, and I will bring judgment against your children's children, said the Lord.
And now cross over to the regions of Kittim and see; send to Kedar and take careful note whether such [?] things have ever happened.
Have the nations changed their gods, though those are not gods? But my people has exchanged my glory for that which will be of no profit to it.
And the heavens were amazed at this, and the earth trembled greatly, said the Lord.
For my people has committed two evils: they have forsaken me, the fountain of living water, and dug out for themselves [?] cisterns that cannot hold water.
Is Israel a slave? Or is Jacob a [?] (house-born slave?), that he has become plunder?
Over him lions roared and gave forth their voice. They made his land a ruin, and his cities were overthrown and left without inhabitants.
Moreover, the sons of Memphis and Tahpanhes have known you and mocked you. What has your forsaking of me done to you?
says the Lord.
And now what have you to do with the way of Egypt, to drink the water of Gihon? And what have you to do with the way of Assyria, to drink the water of its rivers?

Your apostasy will teach you a lesson, and your wickedness will rebuke you. Understand and see that it is bitter and evil for you to forsake me, said the Lord your God; and I took no pleasure in you, says the Lord your God.

For from the beginning you broke your yoke and burst your bonds, and said, "I will not serve you; I will go up onto every high hill, and under every shady tree I will pour myself out there in my fornication."
But I planted you as a fruitful vine, wholly true. How have you turned into bitterness, you strange vine?
And even if you wash yourself with nitre and use much soap to cleanse yourself, you are still defiled in your iniquities before me, said the Lord.
How can you say, "I am not defiled, and I have not gone after Baal"? Look at your ways in the burial grounds, and know what you have done. At evening she lamented in her own voice.

She spread out her ways over the waters of the wilderness; she was [?] by the desire of her soul. She has given herself over; who will turn her back? All who seek her will not grow weary; they will find her in her humiliation.
Turn back your feet from the rough way, and your throat from thirst. But she said, "I will be strong, and I will not obey you," for she loved strangers and followed after them.
As a thief is ashamed when he is caught, so will the sons of Israel be ashamed: they, and their kings, and their princes, and their priests, and their prophets.

They said to a piece of wood, "You are my father," and to a stone, "You gave birth to me." They turned their backs to me and not their faces. Yet in the time of their trouble they will say, "Arise and save us."

So where are the gods that you made? Let them arise and save you in the time of your distress. For your gods were as many as your cities, Judah, and they sacrificed to Baal as many times as there are streets going out of Jerusalem.
Why do you speak to me? All of you have become ungodly, and all of you have acted lawlessly against me, says the Lord.
I struck down your children for nothing; you did not accept correction. The sword devoured your prophets like a destroying lion, and you were not afraid.

Hear the word of the Lord. Thus says the Lord: Have I become a wilderness to the house of Israel, or a land left fallow? Why did my people say, "We will be without a lord, and we will not come to you again"?
Will a bride forget her jewelry, or a virgin the ornament on her breast, her girdle? Yet my people have forgotten me for days beyond number.
Now what good will you devise in your ways to seek love? Not so; instead you too have done evil by defiling your ways.
And the blood of innocent souls was found on your hands. I did not find them while they were digging through a wall; I found them under every oak.
And you said, "I am innocent; let his anger turn away from me." Look, I will judge you, because you said, "I have not sinned."

For I [?] was greatly despised in the [?] of your ways. You will be put to shame by Egypt too, just as you were put to shame by Assyria. From there too you will go out with your hands on your head, because the Lord has rejected the things you put your hope in, and you will not prosper through them.

If a man divorces his wife, and she leaves him and becomes another man's, will she ever return to him again? Will that woman not be utterly defiled? And you have played the harlot with many shepherds, and yet you return to me, says the Lord.
Lift up your eyes and see: where have you not been defiled? You sat by the roads and waited, like a lone crow in the wilderness. You defiled the land with your harlotry and your wickedness.
And you had many shepherds as a stumbling block to you. You had the face of a harlot; you became shameless toward everyone.
Did you not call me your house, and your father, and the lord of your virginity?
Will it last forever, or will it be kept until victory? Look, you said this, and you did this evil, and you prevailed.

And the Lord said to me in the days of King Josiah: "Have you seen what the inhabitants of Israel have done to me? They went up onto every high mountain and under every leafy tree, and they played the harlot there."
And after she had played the harlot I said, "Return to me," but she did not return. And her lawless sister Judah saw her falseness.

And I saw that for all the things in which she had fallen away, in which the dwelling of Israel had committed adultery, I sent her away and gave her a bill of divorce into her hands. Yet her lawless sister Judah was not afraid; she went and played the harlot as well.
And her harlotry became as nothing to her; she defiled the land and committed adultery with wood and stone.
Yet in all this her faithless sister Judah did not return with her whole heart, but only in falsehood.
And the Lord said to me: Faithless Israel has proved herself more righteous than lawless Judah.

Go and read out these words toward the north, and say: Return to me, people living in Israel, says the Lord, and I will not set my face against you, for I am merciful, says the Lord, and I will not be angry with you forever.

But recognize your lawlessness, for you have been ungodly toward the Lord your God, and you have multiplied your ways toward strangers under every leafy tree, and you did not listen to my voice, says the Lord.
Return, faithless children, says the Lord, for I will be lord over you, and I will take you, one from a city and two from a family, and I will bring you to Zion.
And I will give you shepherds after my own heart, and they will shepherd you with knowledge.

And when you multiply and increase on the earth, said the Lord, in those days, says the Lord, they will no longer say, "The ark of the covenant of the Holy One of Israel." It will not come to mind, nor will it be named, nor will it be sought again, nor will it be made again.

And in those days and at that time they will call Jerusalem the throne of the Lord, and all the nations will gather there, to Jerusalem, in the name of the Lord, and they will no longer follow the desires of their evil heart.
In those days the house of Judah will join the house of Israel, and together they will come from the north, from all the lands, to the land that I gave as an inheritance to their fathers.
And I said: So be it, Lord. For I made you my children and gave you a chosen land, the glorious inheritance of God Almighty. And I said to you: Call me Father, and do not turn away from me.
But as a wife is unfaithful to her companion, so the house of Israel and the house of Judah have been unfaithful to me, says the Lord.
A voice was heard from lips, of the weeping and pleading of the sons of Israel, for they had acted lawlessly in their ways and had forgotten their holy God.
Return, children, return, and I will heal your wounds. Here we are, we will be yours, for you are our God.
Truly the hills and the strength of the mountains were a lie, but the salvation of the house of Israel comes from the Lord our God.
And shame has devoured what our fathers worked for since our youth: their flocks and their calves, their sons and their daughters.
We lie down in our shame, and our disgrace has covered us, for we have sinned before our Lord, we and our fathers, from our youth until this day, and we have not listened to the voice of our God.
If Israel returns, said the Lord, let him return to me; and if he removes the abominations from his mouth and stands in awe before my face,
and swears, "As the Lord lives," in truth, justice and righteousness, then the nations will bless him, and through him they will praise God in Jerusalem.
For thus says the Lord to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Break up your fallow ground, and do not sow among thorns.

Circumcise yourselves to your God, and circumcise your hearts, men of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem. Otherwise my anger will break out like fire and blaze up, and there will be no one to put it out, because of the wickedness of your ways.
Declare it in Judea, and let it be heard in Jerusalem. Say: Sound the trumpets across the land; cry out loudly and say:
“Gather together and go into the fortified cities. Get up and flee to Zion; hurry and do not stop, for I am bringing evil from the north, and great destruction.”
A lion has come out of his lair to destroy the nations. He has set out and left his place to make your land a desolation, and your cities have fallen, because there was no one to build them up.
For this, put on sackcloth, beat your breasts and lament, for the wrath of the Lord's anger has not turned away from you.
And on that day, says the Lord, the heart of the king and the heart of the princes will fail, the priests will be dismayed, and the prophets will be astonished.
And I said: “O Lord, Lord, have you really deceived this people and Jerusalem with a lie? For you said, ‘You will have peace’; and now the sword has reached their very soul.”
At that time it will be said to this people and to Jerusalem: “A spirit of error is in the wilderness; the way of the daughter of my people is neither pure nor holy.”
A spirit of fullness will come to me from them; now I too will pronounce my judgment against them.
Look, he will come up like a cloud, and his chariots are like a whirlwind. His horses are swifter than eagles. Woe to us, for we have been ruined!
Jerusalem, wash the wickedness from your heart, so that you may be saved. How long will thoughts of your sorrows remain within you?
For the sound of a cry will come from Dan, and anguish will be heard from the princes of Ephraim.
Remind the nations: look, they are coming to Jerusalem. Declare it: a band is coming from a distant land, and they have raised their voice against the cities of Judah.
They have surrounded her like watchmen guarding a field, because you have treated me with contempt, says the Lord.
Your ways and your doings have brought this on you. This is your wickedness: it is bitter for you, for it has reached your heart.
My belly, my belly aches, and so do the senses of my heart! My soul groans, and my heart is torn; I cannot keep silent, for my soul has heard the sound of the trumpet, the shout of battle
and of misery. It calls out destruction, for the whole land has become wretched. Suddenly my tent was brought low, and my courts were torn apart.
How long must I see fugitives and hear the sound of trumpets?
For the rulers of my people have not known me. They are foolish children without understanding. They are clever at doing evil, but they do not know how to do good.
I looked at the earth, and nothing could be seen; and at the sky, and it had no light.
I looked at the mountains, and they were trembling, and all the hills were shaking.
I looked, and there was no one there, and all the birds of the sky were [?] (perhaps “terrified” or “gone”).
I looked, and Carmel was a wasteland. All the cities had been burned with fire before the Lord, and they were destroyed before the wrath of his anger.
Thus says the Lord: The whole land will become a wilderness, but I will not make [?] (perhaps “a complete end”) of it.
Let the earth mourn, and let the heaven above be darkened, for I have said it: I am resolved, and I will not repent; I have set out, and I will not turn back from it.
At the sound of the horsemen and of the drawn bows the whole land fled. They went into caves, hid in the thickets, and climbed up onto the rocks, and every city was abandoned. No one lives in them.

And you, wretched one, what will you do? Even if you dress yourself in purple, adorn yourself with ornaments of gold, and paint your eyes with eye-paint, your beauty will be for nothing. Your lovers have rejected you; they seek your life.

For I have heard a voice like that of a woman in labour, the sound of your groaning like that of a woman giving birth for the first time: the voice of the daughter of Zion. She will faint [?], and her hands will hang loose. Woe is me, for my soul grows faint because of the slain.

Run through the streets of Jerusalem, look and take note, and search its squares to see whether you can find a man there. If even one person can be found who does justice and seeks faithfulness, then I will be merciful to it, says the Lord.
"The Lord lives," they say; and do they not swear falsely by it?

O Lord, your eyes look for faithfulness. You struck them, but they felt no grief; you made an end of them, but they refused to accept instruction. They made their faces harder than stone and refused to turn back.
And I said: "They are poor and powerless, because they have not understood the way of the Lord and the judgement of their God."
I will go to the rich and speak to them, for they have understood the way of the Lord and the judgement of God. But look: all together they have broken the yoke and burst the bonds.

Therefore a lion from the forest has fallen on them, and a wolf has destroyed them right up to their houses, and a leopard has kept watch over their cities. Everyone who goes out of them will be hunted down, for they have multiplied their ungodliness and grown strong in their turning away.

For which of these things should I be merciful to you? Your sons have forsaken me and sworn by those who are not gods, and they made others swear by them [?]. I fed them until they were full, and they committed adultery and lodged in the houses of harlots.
They became stallions mad for mares; each one neighed after his neighbour's wife.
Shall I not punish them for this, says the Lord? Shall my soul not take vengeance on a nation such as this?
Go up on its ramparts and tear them down, but do not make a complete end. Leave its foundations, for they belong to the Lord.
For the house of Israel and the house of Judah have treated me with utter contempt.
They have lied about their Lord, said the Lord. They said, "It is not so. No evil will come upon us, and we will not see sword or famine."
Your prophets were wind, and the word of the Lord was not in them. So let it be done to them.
Therefore thus says the Lord Almighty: Because they have spoken this word, look, I will make my words in your mouth a fire and this people the wood, and it will consume them.

Look, I am bringing a nation from far away against you, O house of Israel, says the Lord. It is an ancient nation, a nation from long ago, a nation whose language you do not know and whose speech you will not understand.
Their quivers are like an open grave. All of them are mighty, and they will devour your harvest,

and your bread; they shall devour your sons and your daughters; they shall devour your sheep and your cattle; they shall devour your vines and your fig trees and your olive trees; and they shall shatter with the sword your fortified cities, in which you trust.
And in those days, says the Lord your God, I will not make a full end of you.

And when you say, "Why has the Lord our God done all this to us?", then say to them: "Because you forsook me and served foreign gods in your land, so you shall serve strangers in a land that is not yours."
Declare this to the house of Jacob, and let it be heard in the house of Judah.
Let this be heard by a foolish and senseless people. They have eyes and do not see; they have ears and do not hear.

Will you not fear me, says the Lord, and will you not tremble before my face? I set the sand as a boundary for the sea forever, and it shall not cross it. It will heave but will not prevail, and its waves will roar but will not cross it.
But this people has a disobedient and rebellious heart; they have turned aside and gone away.

And they did not say in their heart, "Let us fear the Lord our God, who gives us the early rain and the late rain in its season, and who has kept for us, season by season, the appointed times of the fields."
Your iniquities have turned these things away, and because of your sins what is good has been withheld from you.
For ungodly men were found among my people, and they set snares to destroy people, and they caught them.

Like a snare that is set and full of birds, so their houses are full of deceit. Therefore they have become great and rich; they have grown fat and sleek, and in their wickedness they have transgressed my words.
They did not judge with justice, and they did not decide the cause of the orphan and the widow.
Shall I not punish them for these things, says the Lord? Shall my soul not take vengeance on a nation such as this?
An astonishing and horrible thing has happened in the land.
The prophets prophesied falsely, and the priests applauded them with their hands, and my people loved it so. And what will you do when the end of this comes?
Be strong, sons of Benjamin, in the midst of Jerusalem! Sound the trumpet in Tekoa, and raise a signal over Beth-haccherem, for evil has appeared from the north, and there shall be great destruction
upon the beautiful and the delicate one; and that righteousness of yours shall be taken from you, O daughter of Zion.
Shepherds will come there with their flocks, and they will pitch tents against her all around, and each will pasture his own flock with his own hand.
"Prepare for battle against her! Rise, and let us go up there at noon!" "Woe to us, for the day has declined, for the shadows of the sea [?] are fading."
"Rise, and let us go up by night, and let us destroy her foundations."
For thus says the Lord of hosts: Cut down her trees; bring a force against Jerusalem, against that city that is utterly false, for there is oppression within her.
As a cistern keeps its water cool, so her wickedness keeps her cool. Ungodliness and misery are heard within her, before her face continually, with pain and blows.
Be instructed, O Jerusalem, lest my soul be estranged from you, and I make you a pathless land where no one can live.
For thus says the Lord of hosts: Glean, glean the remnant of Israel as one gleans a vine. Put your hand back again, as the grape-gatherer does to his basket.

To whom shall I speak and bear witness, so that he may hear? Behold, their ears are uncircumcised, and they cannot hear. Behold, the word of the Lord has become a reproach to them; they do not wish to hear it at all.

And I have filled up my wrath and held it back, and I have not finished them off. I will pour it out on the infants outside and on the gatherings of young men together; for husband and wife will be seized together, the old man with the one who is full of days.
Their houses will pass over and be seized by strangers, their fields and their wives together; and I will stretch out my hand against the inhabitants of this land, says the Lord.
For from the least of them to the greatest of them, all have committed lawlessness; from the priest to the false prophet, all have practised falsehood.
And they have been healing the wounds of my people with wickedness; they have despised me and said, 'Peace, peace,' and where is peace?

They were put to shame because they failed, and yet they were not abashed as those who feel shame are, and they did not perceive their disgrace. Therefore they will fall in their ruin, and at the time of their visitation they will grow weak, said the Lord.

Thus says the Lord: Stand upon the road and look, and ask about the everlasting paths of the Lord, and understand which is the good way, and walk in it, and you will find purity for your souls. And they said, 'We will not go.'
And I set watchmen over you: 'Hear the sound of the trumpet!' And they said, 'We will not hear.'
Therefore the nations heard, and those who shepherd their flocks among them.
Hear, O earth: behold, I will send upon this people according to the fruit of their apostasy, for they did not heed my words, and they have put away my law.
Why do you bring me incense from Sheba, and cinnamon from a far-off land? Your whole burnt offerings are not acceptable, and your sacrifices have not pleased me.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will bring weakness upon this people, and fathers and sons together will grow weak in it; a neighbour and his companion will perish.
Thus says the Lord of hosts: Behold, a people is coming from the north, and a great nation and many kings will rise up from the ends of the earth.
Archers and spearmen, it is ruthless and will not have mercy on you. Their voice roars like the sea; with horses and chariots they are drawn up like fire for battle against you, O daughter of Zion.
We have heard the report of them, and our hands have grown slack; affliction has seized us, pangs like those of a woman in childbirth.
Do not go out into the fields, and do not walk on the roads, for the sword of the enemies is settled all around.
O daughter of my people, gird on sackcloth and pour ashes over yourself; as in mourning for a beloved one, make bitter lamentation for yourself, for suddenly misery will come upon you.
I have set you as a tester among my people who are held back, and you shall understand and test their way.
All of them are disobedient and walk crookedly; like bronze and iron, all of them are corrupted.
The bellows have failed in the fire, the lead has failed; in vain does the silversmith work the silver. Their wickednesses have not melted away.
Call them untested silver, for the Lord has rejected them.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, and he said:
Stand in the gates of the house of the Lord, and read out this word there, and say: Hear the word of the Lord, all Judea, you who enter these gates to worship the Lord.
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Make your ways and your conduct right, and I will let you dwell in this place.
Do not put your trust in yourselves or in lying words, for they will do you no good at all. They say: "The temple of the Lord, the temple of the Lord it is."
For if you truly make your ways and your conduct right, and truly do justice between a man and his neighbour,
and do not oppress the stranger, the orphan and the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place, and do not follow other gods, to your own harm,
then I will let you dwell in this place, the land that I gave to your fathers from of old and for ever.
But if you trust in yourselves, relying on lying words that will not profit you at all,
and you steal, and murder, and commit adultery, and swear falsely, and burn incense to Baal, and go after other gods whom you have not known,
so that evil comes upon you, and then you come and stand before me in the house over which my name has been called, and say, "We have kept ourselves from doing all these abominations":
has my house, over which my name has been called, become a den of robbers in your eyes? And now, behold, I have seen it, says the Lord.
Go to my place that was in Shiloh, where I first made my name dwell, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of my people Israel.
And now, because you have done all these things, says the Lord, and I spoke to you, rising early and speaking to you, and you did not listen to me, and I called you and you did not answer me,
I will do to this house, over which my name is called and in which you trust, and to this place that I gave to you and to your fathers, what I did to Shiloh.
And I will cast you out of my sight, as I cast out your brothers, the whole race of Ephraim.
And now, you: do not pray for this people, do not plead with me to have mercy on them, do not bow down, and do not come to me on their behalf, for I will not listen to you.
Do you not see what they are doing in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem?

Their sons gather wood, and their fathers light the fire, and their women knead dough to make cakes for the host of heaven, and they pour out drink offerings to foreign gods, so that they may provoke me to anger.
Is it I whom they provoke to anger, says the Lord? Is it not themselves, to the shame of their own faces?

Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, my anger and my wrath will be poured out on this place, on people and on cattle, on every tree of the field and on all the fruit of the earth, and it will burn and will not be quenched.
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Gather your whole burnt offerings together with your sacrifices.
For I did not speak to your fathers or command them about whole burnt offerings and sacrifices on the day when I brought them up out of the land of Egypt,
But this is the word I commanded them, and I said: "Listen to my voice, and I will be your God and you will be my people. Walk in all my ways that I command you, so that it may go well with you."
But they did not listen to me, and they did not turn their ear to me. Instead they walked in the plans of their own wicked hearts, and they went backward and not forward.
From the day their fathers came out of the land of Egypt until this very day, I have sent you all my servants the prophets, by day; I sent them early in the morning.
But they did not listen to me, and they did not turn their ear to me. They stiffened their necks and did more evil than their fathers.
You will speak this word to them, but they will not listen to you. You will call to them, but they will not answer you.
And say to them: "This is the nation that did not listen to the voice of the Lord God and did not accept instruction. Faithfulness has failed, and it has been taken away from their mouths."
Shave your head and throw the hair away, and take up a lament on your lips, for the Lord has rejected and cast off the generation that does these things.
For the sons of Judah have done evil before me, says the Lord. They have set up their abominations in my house, which is called by my name, in order to defile it.

They have built the high places of Tophet, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and daughters in fire. I did not command them to do this, and I never planned it in my heart.

Therefore, behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when people will no longer say "the high places of Tophet" or "the valley of the son of Hinnom," but "the valley of the slain." They will bury the dead in Tophet, because there will be no other place for them.
The corpses of this people will be food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth, and there will be no one to drive them away.

I will take away from the cities of Judah and from the streets of Jerusalem the sound of merrymaking, the sound of rejoicing, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, for the land will become a desolation.

At that time, says the Lord, they will bring out of their tombs the bones of the kings of Judah, the bones of their princes, the bones of the priests, the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the dead of Jerusalem.

They will spread them out before the sun and the moon, before all the stars and all the host of heaven, which they loved, served, followed after, heeded and worshipped. The bones will not be gathered up or buried. They will be a disgrace on the face of the earth.
For they chose death rather than life. Death will be more desirable than life to all the remnant left of that wicked nation, in every place where I have driven them, says the Lord of hosts.
And say to them: "Thus says the Lord: When someone falls, does he not get up again? When someone turns away, does he not turn back?"
Why then has my people turned away like this, and Jerusalem turned away so shamelessly? They have held fast to their own thoughts and refused to return.

Pay attention and listen: do they not speak like this? There is no one who repents of his wickedness and says, "What have I done?" The runner has not slowed his running, like a sweating horse neighing as it charges,

The stork in the sky knew its season; the turtledove, the swallow, the crane [?], and the sparrows of the field kept the times of their coming. But my people did not understand the judgments of the Lord.
How can you say, 'We are wise, and the law of the Lord is with us'? The scribes' portion of falsehood was in vain.
The wise were put to shame; they were dismayed and were caught [?], because they despised the word of the Lord. What wisdom is in them?

Therefore I will give their wives to others and their fields to foreign heirs, because from the least of them to the greatest, all ran after greed. From the prophet to the priest, everyone commits lawlessness.
They tried to heal the wound of the daughter of my people, treating me with contempt, and they said, 'Peace, peace,' when there is no peace.

They were put to shame because they did what was detestable, yet even so they felt no shame and did not know how to blush. Therefore they will fall among the fallen, and in the time of their visitation they will be brought down, said the Lord.
They will gather their fruits, said the Lord, but there are no grapes on the vines and no figs on the fig trees, and the leaves have fallen. What I gave them has passed away from them.
Why do we sit still? Gather together, and let us go into the fortified cities and perish there, for the Lord God has cast us off and given us bitter water to drink, because we have sinned before him.
We gathered for peace, but no good came; we waited for a time of healing, and look, there is distress.

From Dan we heard the noise of his many horses. At the sound of the neighing of his mounted horses the whole land will shake. He will come and devour the land and everything in it, the city and those who live in it.
For look, I will send deadly serpents among you, which cannot be charmed, and they will bite you, says the Lord.
With incurable pain in your maddened hearts.

Listen, the sound of the daughter of my people crying out from a distant land: 'Is the Lord not in Zion? Is her king not there?' Why have they provoked me to anger with their idols and with worthless foreign things?
The harvest is past, the threshing is finished, and we have not been saved.
I am broken over the breaking of the daughter of my people. I am darkened with dismay; pains have seized me like those of a woman in childbirth.
Is there no balm in Gilead? Is there no physician there? Why then has no healing come to the daughter of my people?
If only someone would make my head water and my eyes a fountain of tears, so that I could weep day and night for this people, for the wounds of the daughter of my people.
If only someone would give me a small lodging in the desert, so that I could leave this people of mine and go away from them, for they all commit adultery; they are a gang of the lawless.
They bent their tongues like bows. Falsehood, not faithfulness, has grown strong in the land, for they have gone from evil to evil, and they did not know me, says the Lord.
Let each of you beware of his neighbor, and do not trust your brothers, for every brother deceives with lies and every friend goes about in treachery.
Each one mocks his friend; they do not speak the truth. They have taught their tongues to speak lies. They plunder and do not stop long enough to turn back.
Interest upon interest and deceit upon deceit; they refused to know me, said the Lord.
Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts: Behold, I will refine them and test them, for what else shall I do because of the wickedness of the daughter of my people?
Their tongue is a wounding arrow; the words of their mouth are deceitful. A man speaks peace to his neighbour, but in his heart he lays up enmity.
Shall I not punish them for this, says the Lord? Or shall my soul not take vengeance on a nation such as this?

Raise a sound of weeping upon the mountain, and lamentation upon the paths of the wilderness, for they have been left desolate, because no people pass through them. The sound of livestock is no longer heard there; from the birds of the sky to the cattle, they have [?] and perished.
And I will give Jerusalem up to be plundered and to be a dwelling-place for dragons, and I will lay waste the cities of Judah and make them ruins without inhabitant.

Who is the wise man who will understand this? And with whom is the word of the mouth of the Lord, that he may tell you why the land has perished and has been left like a wilderness, with no one passing through it?
And the Lord said to me: Because they forsook my law, which I set before their face, and did not listen to my voice, and did not walk in it,
but walked in the ways of the will of their evil heart and in the way of the idols, which their fathers taught them,
therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will feed them with anguish, and give them water of bitterness to drink.
And I will scatter them among the nations whom neither they nor their fathers have known, and I will send the sword upon them until I have consumed them by it.
Thus says the Lord of hosts: Consider, and call for the mourning women, and let them come; and send for the skilled women, and let them raise laments over you, and let them make haste.
And let them take up lamentation over you; let your eyes shed tears, and let your eyelids pour out water.
For a pitiful voice has been heard in Zion: How we have been made wretched! We have been greatly put to shame, for we have left our land and cast away our dwellings.
Hear now, you women, the word of God, and let your ears receive the words of my mouth; teach your daughters a cry of pain, and let each woman teach her neighbour lamentation.
For death has come up through your windows; it has entered your land to destroy the infants outside, and the young men from the streets, by death.
Thus says the Lord: The corpses of men shall lie as a disgrace upon the face of the fields of your land, like hay behind the mower, and there shall be no one to gather them.
Thus says the Lord: Let not the wise man boast in his wisdom, nor let the mighty man boast in his strength, and let not the rich man boast in his riches.

But let him who boasts boast in this: in understanding and knowing me, that I am the Lord who has done mercy and judgment and righteousness on the earth; for in these things is my will, says the Lord.
Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will punish all the circumcised for their circumcision:

Egypt, and Judea, and Edom, and the sons of Ammon, and the sons of Moab, and all who cut the hair at the sides of their faces, who dwell in the wilderness. For all the nations are uncircumcised, and the whole house of Israel is uncircumcised in heart.
Hear the word that the Lord has spoken concerning you, O house of Israel.
Thus says the Lord: Do not learn the ways of the nations, and do not be afraid of the signs of heaven, for they are afraid before their face.
For the law of the nations is vain: it is a tree cut from the forest, the work of a craftsman,
and cast. They are adorned with gold [?] and silver; with hammers and nails they fastened them, so that they would not move.
It is embossed silver, and it does not walk.
Poured silver brought from Tarshish, gold from Uphaz, by the hands of goldsmiths, all of it the work of skilled craftsmen; they clothe them in blue and scarlet.
They have to be lifted up and carried, for they cannot walk. Do not be afraid of them, for they can do no harm, and there is no good in them either.
Who is like you, O Lord? You are great, and your name is great in your might.
Who would not fear you, O King of the nations? For worship is fitting for you. Among all the wise men of the nations and among their kings, who is like you, O Lord?
All together they became senseless and foolish, for the teaching of vain things among them is wood.
Beaten silver brought from Tarshish, and gold from Ophir, the work of a craftsman and of the hands of goldsmiths; blue and scarlet is their clothing, all of it the work of skilled men.
But the Lord is the true God, the living God and the eternal King. At his wrath the earth will quake, and the nations cannot endure his fury.
Thus you shall say to them: The gods who did not make heaven and earth, let them perish from the earth and from under this heaven.
It is the Lord who made the earth by his power; he established the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding he stretched out the heavens.
He gives voice, and there is a multitude of waters in heaven; he brings up clouds from the ends of the earth; he made lightnings for the rain, and he brought forth winds from his storehouses.
Every man has become foolish, without knowledge, and every goldsmith is put to shame by his carved images, for he has cast a falsehood; there is no breath in them.
Those works are vain, worthy of mockery; at the time of their visitation they will perish.
The portion of Jacob is not like these. Rather, the one who created all things is himself his portion, and Israel is the rod of his inheritance; the Lord of hosts is his name.
He has gathered your strength from round about, you who dwell among the chosen,
for thus says the Lord: I will make the inhabitants of this land stumble with affliction, and I will afflict them so that it may be shown to them; it has been found.
Woe for your shattering! Painful is this wound of yours. And I said: Truly this wound is mine, and it has come upon me.

My tent has been made wretched and has perished, and all my courts have been torn apart. My children and my flock have gone away from me; there is no longer any place for my tent, nor any place for my courts.
For the shepherds acted foolishly and did not seek the Lord; therefore none of their flock understood, but they were scattered.
Behold, the sound of a report is coming, and a great quaking from the land of the north, to make the cities of Judah a ruin and a nesting place for ostriches.
I know, O Lord, that a man's way is not his own, and a man does not walk and direct his own way or make his steps go straight.
Correct us, O Lord, but with judgment and not in anger, so that you do not diminish us.
Pour out your wrath on the nations that do not know you, and on the kings who have not called on your name. For they have devoured Jacob and finished him off, and laid waste his pasture.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
"Hear the words of this law, and speak to all the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
And say to them: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Cursed be the man who does not listen to the words of this law,

which I commanded your fathers on the day I brought them up out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron furnace. I said: Listen to my voice, and do everything that I command you. Then I will be your God, and you will be my people,
so that I may establish the oath I swore to your fathers, to give them a land flowing with milk and honey, as it is this day." And I answered and said, "So be it, O Lord."
And the Lord said to me: "Proclaim these words in the cities of Judah and around Jerusalem, and say: Hear the words of this law, and do them.
For I solemnly warned your fathers on the day I brought them up out of the land of Egypt, and up to this day. I rose early, warned them and said: Listen to my voice.

But they did not listen and did not incline their ears. Each one walked in the stubbornness of his evil heart. So I brought on them all the words of this law, which I had commanded them to do and which they did not do."
And the Lord said to me: "A conspiracy has been found among the men of Judah and among the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

They have turned back to the iniquities of their forefathers, who refused to hear my words. And see, they go after foreign gods to serve them. The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken my covenant, which I made with their fathers.
Therefore thus says the Lord: See, I will bring evils on them that they will not be able to escape. They will cry out to me, and I will not listen to them.
And the cities of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem will go and cry out to the gods to whom they burn incense, but these will not save them at all in the time of their affliction.
For your gods, O Judah, were as many as your cities, and you set up altars of shame to burn incense to Baal, as many as the streets of Jerusalem.
As for you, do not pray for this people, and do not plead with me for them with prayer and worship, for I will not listen to them at the time when they call on me, in the time of their affliction.
Why has your beloved done an abomination in my house? Shall vows and holy flesh take away your wickedness from you? Or will you escape by these things?
The Lord called your name a beautiful olive tree, shady to look at. At the sound of circumcision a fire blazed up upon it; great affliction is upon you; your branches have become worthless.

The Lord of hosts, who planted you, has pronounced evil against you because of the wickedness of the house of Israel and the house of Judah. For they did it of their own accord to provoke me to anger, when they burned incense to Baal."
O Lord, give me understanding, and I will know, for then I saw their schemes.

But I was like an innocent lamb led [?] to slaughter, and I did not know it. They plotted an evil plan against me and said: "Come, let us put wood into his bread, and let us cut him off from the land of the living, so that his name is remembered no more."
But you, O Lord of hosts, righteous judge, who test hearts and kidneys: let me see your vengeance on them, for to you I have laid open my cause.
Therefore thus says the Lord about the men of Anathoth who seek my life, who say: "Do not prophesy in the name of the Lord, or you will die by our hands."
Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts: Behold, I will take vengeance on them. Their young men shall be cut down by the sword, and their sons and their daughters shall die of famine.
And none of them shall be left, for I will bring evil upon the inhabitants of Anathoth in the year of their punishment.
You are righteous, O Lord, and I will plead my case with you, yet I will speak to you of judgments: why does the way of the ungodly prosper? All who deal falsely with you in falsehood are at ease.
You planted them, and they took root; they had children and bore fruit. You are near in their mouth, but far from their kidneys.
And you, O Lord, know me; you have seen me and tested my heart before you. Gather them like sheep for slaughter, and set them apart for the day of their slaughter.

How long shall the land mourn, and all the grass of the field wither because of the wickedness of those who live in the land? The beasts and the birds have been destroyed [?] if God has not seen our ways.
Your feet run, and they will wear you out; how will you get ready to go against horses? And you do not trust in a land of peace; how then will you do in the swelling of the Jordan?

For even your brothers and your father's house, even they have dealt falsely with you, and they too have shouted after you and gathered against you. Do not believe them, for they speak good things to you.
I have forsaken my house; I have abandoned my inheritance. I have given my beloved soul into the hands of her enemies.
My inheritance has become like a lion in a forest; it has raised its voice against me. Therefore I have hated it.
Is not my inheritance to me a hyena's den, or a cave around it? Go, gather all the beasts of the field, and let them come to devour it.
Many shepherds have ruined my vineyard; they have made my desired portion a trackless wilderness.
It has been made a thing for ruin and destruction. Because of me the whole land has been utterly ruined, for there is no one who takes this to heart.

Upon all the places of the desert the wretched have come into the wilderness, for the sword of the Lord shall devour from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth. There is no peace for any flesh.
Sow wheat and reap thorns. Your portions shall not profit you. Be ashamed of your boasting, because of the reproach before God.

For thus says the Lord about all your neighbours, the evil shepherds who harm my inheritance, which I gave as a portion to my people Israel: Behold, I will pluck them up from their land, and I will bring the house of Judah out from among them.
And it shall be, when I have brought them out, I will turn back and have mercy on them, and I will settle them each in his own inheritance, and every man in his own land.

And it shall be, if they diligently teach my people my way, to swear by my name, 'As the Lord lives,' just as they taught my people to swear by Baal, then they shall be built up in the midst of my people.
But if they do not turn back, I will destroy that nation with utter destruction and ruin, said the Lord.
Thus the Lord said to me: Go and get yourself a linen [?] girdle and gird it around your loins, and it has not been washed in water.
And I got the girdle, as the Lord told me, and girded it around my loins.
And the word of the Lord came to me a second time, and he said to me:
Take that girdle of yours which you got, which is on your loins, and arise and go to the bank of the Euphrates, and hide it there in a hole in the rock.
And I went and hid it by the bank of the Euphrates, as the Lord commanded me.
And it came to pass after many days that the Lord said to me: Arise and go to the Euphrates, and take from there the girdle which I commanded you to hide there.
And I went to the Euphrates; I dug and took the girdle from the place where I had buried it, and behold, it was ruined there, so that it was no longer useful for anything.
And the word of the Lord came to me, and he said to me:
Thus says the Lord: Thus have I ruined the pride of Judah and the pride of Jerusalem.
This is great pride: this wicked people, who did not want to hear my words, and who walk in the self-will [?] of their evil heart, and who walk after foreign gods, to serve them and to worship them.

And they shall be like this girdle, which is no longer useful for anything. For as a girdle clings to a man's loins, so I brought near to myself the house of Israel and all the house of Judah, said the Lord, to be a renowned people, a boast, and a glory; and they did not listen to me.

And now say to this people this word: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Every wineskin shall be filled with wine. And it shall be, if they say to you, 'Do we not surely know that every wineskin shall be filled with wine?'

Then say to them: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will fill all the inhabitants of this land, and the kings, the sons of David, who sit on his thrones, and the priests and the prophets, and Judah and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, I will fill with drunkenness.

And I will scatter them, a man from his brother, and their fathers together, says the Lord. I will not long for them, nor will I spare them, nor will I have mercy on them to save them from their destruction.
Hear and give ear, and do not be lifted up with pride, for the Lord has spoken:

Give glory to the Lord our God before it grows dark, and before your feet are cut off [? i.e. stumble] on the darkened mountains. You will wait for light, and there will be the shadow of death, and you will be plunged into darkness.
And if you do not listen to him, your soul will weep in secret because of pride, and will weep bitterly with tears, and your eyes will pour down tears, for the flock of the Lord has been crushed.
Say to the king and to those who rule over you: Humble yourselves and sit down, for the crown of your glory has been stripped from your head.
The cities toward the south have been shut up, and there was no one to open them. Judah has been carried away captive; they have carried out a complete deportation [?] as retribution.
Lift up your eyes, Jerusalem, and see those who are coming from the north. Where is your flock that was given to you, the sheep of your glory?
What will you say when they visit you? You yourself taught them to rule over you as your head. Pains will seize you like a woman giving birth.
And if you say in your heart, "Why have these things happened to me?" It is because of the great number of your iniquities that your skirts have been lifted up, so that your heels are exposed.
If the Indian can change his skin and the leopard its spots, then you too, who have learned evil, will be able to do good.
And I have scattered you like chaff carried off by the wind into the desert.
This is your lot and the portion for your disobedience toward me, says the Lord, because you forgot me and trusted in falsehood.
And I will lift your skirts up over your face, and your disgrace will be seen.

Your adulteries and your neighing and the strangeness of your fornication: I have seen your abominations on the hills and in the fields. Woe to you, Jerusalem, for you have not been made clean by following me. How long will it still be for you?
And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah about the drought.
Judea has gone into mourning, and her gates are empty. Darkness has come over the land, and the cry of Jerusalem has gone up.

And their rich men sent their young men for water. They went to the cisterns and found no water, and they brought their vessels back empty. They were ashamed and humiliated, and they covered [?] their heads.
And the work of the land failed, for there was no rain on the land. The farmers were ashamed and covered their heads.
Even the deer gave birth [?] in the field and abandoned their fawns, for there was no green grass.
Wild asses stood on the plains and sniffed the wind like dragons. Their eyes failed, for there was no grass.
Even if our sins stand against us, O Lord, show mercy for your name's sake. Our sins are many before you, because we have sinned against you.
O Lord, patience of Israel, you saved us in the time of distress. Why have you become like a stranger in the land, and like a native who turns aside to his lodging?
Do not be like a man asleep, like a man who is unable to save. You are among us, O Lord, and your name is called upon us. Do not forget us.

This is what the Lord says about this people: They have loved to move their feet, and they did not hold them back. And God took no pleasure in them. Now he will remember their iniquities and will punish their sins.
And the Lord said to me: Do not pray for this people's good.

Even if they fast, I will not listen to their prayer. Even if they offer whole burnt offerings and sacrifices, I will not take pleasure in them. Instead, I will destroy them with sword, famine and death.

And I said: "O you who are the sovereign Lord, look: their prophets tell them, 'You will not see the sword, and there will be no famine among you. Instead, I will give truth and peace to the land and to this place.'"

And the Lord said to me: [?] the prophets prophesy in my name. I did not send them, I did not command them, and I did not speak to them. They are prophesying to you false and empty visions and the wishes of their own hearts.

Therefore thus says the Lord: As for the prophets who prophesy in my name, though I did not send them, who say, "Sword and famine shall not come upon this land": those prophets shall perish by death and by a wasting disease, by the sword and by famine.

And the people to whom they prophesied shall be thrown out in the streets of Jerusalem because of the sword and the famine. There shall be no one to bury them: them, their wives, their sons and their daughters. And I will pour out their evil upon them.
And say this word to them: Let your eyes shed tears day and night, and let them not stop, for the virgin daughter of my people has been crushed with a great crushing and with a very grievous wound.
If I go out into the field, there are those slain by the sword; and if I go into the city, there is the pain of famine. For prophet and priest have gone off into a land they did not know.

Have you utterly rejected Judah? Has your soul turned away from Zion? Why have you struck us, so that there is no healing for us? We waited for peace, but there is no good; for a time of healing, but here is terror.
We know, O Lord, our sins and the iniquities of our fathers, for we have sinned before you.
Relent, for your name's sake. Do not destroy the throne of your glory. Remember, and do not break your covenant, which is with us.
Is there any among the idols of the nations who brings rain? Will the sky give its abundance of itself? No, you yourself are the Lord, and we will wait for you, for you made all these things.
And the Lord said to me: Even if Moses and Samuel stood before my face, my soul would not turn toward them. Send this people away, and let them go out.

And if they say to you, "Where shall we go out to?", say to them: Thus says the Lord: Those of you who are mine for death shall die by death; those of you who are mine for the sword shall be slain by the sword; those of you who are mine for famine shall be consumed by famine; and those of you who are mine for captivity shall be carried off captive.
And I will take vengeance on them with four kinds of punishment, says the Lord: the sword to slay, the dogs to tear apart, and the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth to devour and destroy.
And I will give them over to distress among all the kings of the earth, because of Manasseh son of Hezekiah, king of Judah, for all that he did in Jerusalem.
Who will have pity on you, Jerusalem? Who will grieve over you? Or who will turn aside to ask about your welfare?
You turned away from me, says the Lord; you went backward. So I will stretch out my hand against you and destroy you, and I will no longer have mercy on them.
And I will scatter them far and wide. At the gates of my people they have become childless. I destroyed my people because of their wickedness, and they did not turn back.
Their widows have become more numerous than the sand of the seashore. At midday I brought misery upon the mother of young men; I suddenly brought trembling and panic upon her.

And she who bore seven has grown faint; her soul is in anguish. The sun has set on her at the very middle of the day; she is ashamed and disgraced. And I will give what is left of them to the sword before their enemies, said the Lord.

Woe is me, my mother, that you bore me, a man condemned and judged throughout the whole land! I owed nothing to anyone, and no one owed me anything, yet my strength has failed because of those who curse me.
Let it be, O Lord, for their prospering, if I did not stand before you in the time of their evil and in the time of their distress, for good toward the enemy.
Will iron be known? [?] And your wall of bronze is your strength.
And I will give your treasures as plunder in exchange for all your sins, for all your deeds.
And you shall serve your enemies in a land that you do not know, for a fire has been kindled by my anger against you, and it has blazed up.
You know, O Lord. Remember me, O Lord, and look upon me, and clear me before those who pursue me. Do not hold me back in your long-suffering; consider how much reproach I have borne for your sake.
Bring to an end those who despised your words, and let your word be to me a joy and the gladness of my heart, for your name has been called upon me, O Lord Almighty [?].
I did not sit in their assembly while they were making merry, but I was afraid because of your hand; I sat alone, for I was filled with bitterness.
Why do those who harm me prevail over me? My wound has become firmly fixed; from where shall I be healed? It has become to me like deceptive water that cannot be trusted.

Therefore thus says the Lord: If you turn back, I will restore you again, and you shall stand before my face. And if you bring out what is precious from among the unworthy, you shall be as my mouth. They shall turn to you, but you shall not turn to them.
And I will make you to this people like a strong wall of bronze. They will fight against you, but they will not prevail over you, for I am with you to save you and to deliver you, says the Lord.
And I will deliver you from the hands of the wicked, and I will rescue you from the hands of the destroyers. Thus says the Lord God of Israel.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
You shall not take a wife, says the Lord God of Israel, and you shall have neither son nor daughter in this place.
For thus says the Lord about the sons and daughters who are born in this place, and about their mothers who bore them, and about their fathers who begot them in this land:

They shall perish by death and by a [?] disease. They shall not be mourned or buried; they shall be a spectacle on the face of the earth. They shall fall by the sword and be finished off by famine. And their carcasses shall be food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.

Thus says the Lord: Do not enter into their mourning, and do not go to lament them, and do not mourn for them, for I have taken away my peace from this people, says the Lord, and my mercy and my compassion. And great and small shall be destroyed in this land.
They shall not be buried or lamented; no one shall [?] for them or shave their heads, nor weep for them.
And no [?] bread shall be broken in their mourning to comfort them over the dead, nor shall they give him a cup to drink to console him over his father or his mother.
You shall not enter the house of their feasting to sit with them to eat and drink,

for thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, before your eyes and in your days I will banish from this place the voice of delight and the voice of joy, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride.

And when you have told all these words to this people, they will say to you, "Why has the Lord pronounced all this great evil against us? What is our guilt, and what sin have we committed before the Lord our God?"
And say to them: "Because your fathers forsook me, says the Lord, and went after foreign gods, and served them and worshipped them. They forsook me and did not keep my law.
And you have done more evil than your fathers. Behold, each one of you walks after the desire of your wicked heart, so as not to listen to me.
And I will cast you out of this land into a land that neither you nor your fathers have known. There you will serve foreign gods day and night, and they will show you no mercy."
Therefore behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when they will no longer say, "As the Lord lives, who brought the sons of Israel up out of the land of Egypt,"

but, "As the Lord lives, who brought the sons of Israel up out of the land of the north and out of all the lands where he had scattered them." And I will bring them back again to their land, which I gave to their fathers.

Behold, I am sending many fishermen, says the Lord, and they will catch them. And after this I will send many hunters, and they will hunt them on every mountain and on every hill and out of the clefts of the rock.
For my eyes are on all their ways. They are not hidden from my face, and their iniquities cannot be hidden from my eyes.

And first I will repay them double for their iniquities and their sins, because they defiled my land with their carcasses and their abominations, and with their iniquities, with which they filled my inheritance.

O Lord, my strength, my help and my refuge in the day of evil: to you the nations will come from the ends of the earth and say, "The idols our fathers acquired were false, and there is no profit in them.
Can a man make gods for himself? Such things are not gods."
Therefore behold, at this time I will reveal my hand to them, and I will make my power known to them, and they will know that my name is the Lord.
The sin of Judah is written in books of iron with a stylus of adamant. It is engraved on the breast of their hearts and on the edge of their altars, in this way:
when their children remember their offerings, and their sacred groves by the leafy trees, and on the high hills
and the mountains of the plain. I will give your strength and your treasures as plunder, and your high places too, because of your sins, which were throughout all your borders.

And you will be left alone, and stripped of the inheritance that I gave you. And I will make you serve your enemies in my land. And you will understand that a fire has been kindled in my wrath, and it will burn forever.
Thus says the Lord: Cursed is the man who puts his hope in man and trusts in the flesh of his own arm, and whose heart turns away from the Lord.
He will be like a tamarisk of the [?] in the desert, and he will not see it when good comes. He will live in salt-marsh land, in the desert, in a salt land where no one can live.
And blessed is the man who trusts in the Lord;

And he shall be like a fruitful tree by the water, and on moist ground he will fix his roots firmly, and he will not be afraid when the heat comes, and there will be leafy shoots on him in the year of drought. He will not fear, and he will not fail to bring forth fruit.
The heart is deep beyond all things, and it is man, and who can know it?
I, the Lord, examine hearts and test the kidneys, to give to each one according to his ways, and according to the fruits of his deeds.
The partridge called out and gathered [?] which it did not know; [so is one who] makes his wealth without justice: in the middle of his days they will leave him, and at his end he will be a fool.
Exalted throne of glory, our sanctuary, from the beginning the place of holiness for us,
O Patience of Israel, O Lord, let all who have forsaken you be put to shame; let those who have turned away from you be written on the earth, for they have forsaken the fountain of life, the Lord.
Heal me, O Lord, and I shall be healed; save me, and I shall be saved, for you are my boast.
Behold, they say to me, 'Where is the word of the Lord? Let it come to us.'
But I did not grow weary of following in your footsteps, and I did not desire the day of man. You know what comes out of my lips; it is before you.
Do not become a stranger to me; spare me in the evil day.
Let my persecutors be put to shame, and let me not be put to shame; let them be terrified, and let me not be terrified. Bring the evil day upon them; crush them with a double crushing.
Thus the Lord said to me: Go and stand at the gates of the sons of your people, through which the kings of Judah go in and through which they go out, and at all the gates of Jerusalem.
And say to them: Hear the word of the Lord, you kings of Judah, and all Judea, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and you who enter through these gates.
Thus says the Lord: Guard yourselves, and do not take up a burden on the Sabbath day, and do not go out [?] through the gates of Jerusalem.

And do not carry a burden out of your houses on the Sabbath day, and do no work at all, and keep the Sabbath day holy, as I commanded your fathers. But they did not listen, nor did they incline their ear.
And they stiffened their necks more than their fathers did, so as not to obey me and not to accept my instruction.

And it shall be, if you truly listen to me, says the Lord, and do not bring a burden in through the gates of this city on the Sabbath days, and keep the Sabbath days holy by doing no work at all on them,

then kings and princes sitting on the throne of David shall enter this city through these gates, mounted on chariots and on their horses, they and their princes, the princes of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem; and this city shall be inhabited forever.

And they shall come from the cities of Judah, and from the places around Jerusalem, and from Benjamin, and from the plain, and from the hill country, and from the south [?], bringing offerings and incense, manna; and they shall bring frankincense as an offering to the house of the Lord.

But if you do not listen to me, to keep the Sabbath days holy, but take up burdens and enter through the gates of Jerusalem, then I will kindle a fire in its gates, and it shall devour the walls of Jerusalem and shall not be quenched.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, and he said to him:
Arise and go down to the potter's house, and there you shall hear my words.
And I went down to the potter's house, and there he was, doing his work on the stones.
And the vessel that he was making from clay came apart in his hands, and he made it again into another vessel, as it seemed good to him to make them.
And the word of the Lord came to me and said to me: Say to them:
Am I not able to make [you] as this potter [does]? [?] says the Lord. Behold, as clay is in the hand of the potter, so you are in my hands, O house of Israel.
I will pronounce an end against nations and kingdoms, to root them out, to tear them down, and to destroy them.
And if that nation turns from its wickedness, I too will repent of the evils that I planned to do to them.
And I will make a full pronouncement concerning nations and kingdoms, to build them up and to plant them.
And if they do evil before me by not listening to my voice, I too will repent of the good that I said I would do to them.

And now say to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I have prepared evil against you, and I am devising a plan against you. Turn, each of you, from your own evil way, and make your ways and your doings better.
And they said: Let us be strong, and we will walk in the track of our perversity, and each of us will do the will of our evil heart.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Ask even among the nations: who has heard such things as these [?] — the very horrible thing that the virgin of Jerusalem has done?
Will the breasts fail from the rock, or the snow from Lebanon? Will the water be turned back by the violent onrush of the wind?
For my people have forgotten me, and they have burned incense in vain, and they have grown weak from their ways, the everlasting paths, so as to walk in places where there is no road,
to make their land a ruin and a hissing forever. All who pass by will be astonished at it and shake their heads.
Like a scorching wind I will scatter them before the face of their enemies; I will show them my back and not my face on the day of their destruction.

And they said: Come, let us devise a plot against Jeremiah, for the law will not perish from the priest, nor counsel from the wise, nor the word from the prophet. Come, let us strike him with the tongue, and we will listen to all his words.
Hear me, O Lord, and hear the voice of my plea for justice.

Is evil to be repaid to him in return for good? For they have plotted words against my life, and they intend my torment. Remember how I stood before you to speak good on their behalf, so that your anger might be turned away from them.

Therefore give their children over to famine, and deliver them into the hands of the sword. Let their wives become childless and widows, and let their husbands be slain by death, and their young men fall by the sword in battle.
Let there be an outcry in their houses; bring robbers upon them suddenly, for they have begun a plan to seize me, and they have hidden a snare for me.

And you, O Lord, know all their plotting against me to kill me. Do not hold their iniquities guiltless, and do not blot out their sins. Let their weakness be before you; deal with them in the time of your anger.
Then the Lord said to me: Go and buy yourself a jar made by a potter, and bring some of the elders of the people and some of the elders of the priests.
And go out to the burial ground of their children who have died, which is outside the gates of Harsith, and read there all these words that I speak to you.

And he said to them: Hear the word of the Lord, kings of Judah and inhabitants of Jerusalem. Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will bring evil upon this place, so that the ears of everyone who hears of it will ring,

because they have forsaken me and made this place foreign, and burned incense in it to foreign gods whom neither they nor their fathers knew, and the kings of Judah have filled this place with innocent blood.
And they built the high places of Baal, to burn their children with fire as offerings to Baal, which I did not command them, nor did I speak of it, nor did it come into my heart.
Therefore, behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when this place will no longer be called, said the Lord, Place of Falling and Burial Ground of Slaughter [?].

And I will bring to nothing the counsel of Judah and the counsel of Jerusalem in this place, and I will strike them down with the sword before their enemies and by the hand of those who seek their life, and I will give their dead as food to the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.
And I will make this city a ruin and an object of hissing; everyone who passes by will be grieved over it and will hiss because of all its wounds.

And they will eat the flesh of their sons and the flesh of their daughters, and each one will eat the flesh of his neighbor, because of the siege and the distress with which their enemies, and those who seek their lives, will afflict them.
And you shall break the jar before the eyes of the men who went out with you.
And he said to them: Thus says the Lord of hosts: So will I break this people and this city, as an earthen vessel is broken, which can no longer be mended.
Thus will I do to this place, says the Lord, and to those who dwell in it, to make this city like a fallen land.

And the houses of Jerusalem and the houses of the king of Judah will be like a fallen place, because of the uncleanness that they committed in their houses, in which they burned incense on the roofs to all the host of heaven and offered sacrifices to foreign gods. And they will bury in Topheth, for there will be no place for them to bury.
And Jeremiah came from the place of slaughter of Topheth, where the Lord had sent him to prophesy, and he stood in the court of the house of the Lord and said to all the people:

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will bring upon this land, and upon all its cities and its villages, all the evil that I have spoken against it, because they have stiffened their necks so as not to hear my words.
And Pashhur son of Immer, the priest, who was chief officer in the house of the Lord, heard Jeremiah prophesying these words.
And Pashhur struck Jeremiah the prophet and threw him into the dungeon that was at the gate of Benjamin, in the upper house, which was in the house of the Lord.
And on the next day Pashhur brought Jeremiah out of the dungeon, and Jeremiah said to him: The Lord has not called your name Pashhur, but 'Captive All Around.'

For thus says the Lord: Behold, I will hand you over to captivity, you and all your friends. They shall fall by the sword of their enemies, and your eyes shall see it. I will give you and all Judah into the hands of the king of Babylon. He shall carry them captive to Babylon and slay them with the sword.

I will hand over all the wealth of this city, all the fruits of its labour and all its honour. All the treasures of the king of Judah I will give into the hands of their enemies. They shall plunder them, seize them and carry them off to Babylon.

And you, Pashhur, and everyone who lives in your house shall go into captivity. You shall go to Babylon, and there you shall die, and there you shall be buried, you and all your friends to whom you prophesied lies.
You deceived me, O Lord, and I was deceived. You seized me and prevailed. I have become a laughingstock, and I have spent all my days in scorn.
For I laughed with a bitter word. I cried out about falsehood and wretchedness, for the word of the Lord became a reproach and a mockery to me all the days.

And I said, "I will no longer make mention of the name of the Lord, and I will no longer speak in his name." But it became like a blazing fire in my heart, burning and shut up within my bones. I am hemmed in on every side, and I cannot endure it.

For I heard the abuse of many who gathered around me: "Rise up, and let us rise up against him, all you men who are his friends. Let us watch his plans, in case he is led astray. Then we shall prevail over him and take our revenge on him."

But the Lord is with me like a mighty warrior. That is why they persecuted me, yet they could not understand, and they were greatly ashamed, for they did not perceive their own disgrace, which [?] will not be forgotten.
O Lord of hosts, who tests righteousness and knows the hearts and the kidneys, may I see your vengeance upon them, for to you I have laid open my pleas.
Sing to the Lord; praise him, for he has rescued the soul of the poor from the hands of the wicked.
Cursed be the day on which I was born. Let the day on which my mother bore me not be blessed.
Cursed be the man who brought the news to my father and said to him, "A son has been born to you."
Let that man be glad like the cities that the Lord overthrew in anger without relenting. Let him hear wailing in the morning and an outcry at noon,
because he did not kill me in the womb, so that my mother would have become my grave and her womb would have stayed pregnant forever.
Why did I come out of the womb to see toil and sorrow, and to have my days end in shame?
The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah when King Zedekiah sent to him Pashhur son of Malchiah and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah the priest, saying:
"Inquire of the Lord for us, for the king of the Babylonians has come against us. Perhaps the Lord will act according to all his wonders, and he will withdraw from us."
And Jeremiah said to them: "Say this to Zedekiah:
'Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will turn back the weapons of war with which you are fighting the Chaldeans, with which you hold out all around the wall, within this city.
I myself will fight against you with a ready hand and a strong arm, with anger, wrath and great fury.
I will destroy all who live in this city, both people and animals, by a great death.'

And after that, thus says the Lord: I will give Zedekiah, king of Judah, and his servants and his people who are left in this city, to death and famine and the sword, and into the hands of their enemies and of those who seek their lives. They will cut them down with the edge of the sword, and I will not spare them, nor will I have mercy on them.
And to the people he said: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I set before you the way of life and the way of death.
Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword and by famine. But whoever goes out and goes over to the Chaldeans, who have besieged you, will live, and his life will be his as spoil.
For I have set my face against this city for evil and not for good. It will be given into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire.
House of the king of Judah, hear the word of the Lord.
