O house of David, thus says the Lord: Execute judgment in the morning and set things right. Rescue the one who has been robbed from the hand of the one who wrongs him, so that my anger does not break out like fire. It will blaze up, and there will be no one to quench it.
Behold, I am against you who dwell in the valley of Assur, the plain, you who say, “Who will make us tremble, or who will come in to our dwelling?”
I will kindle a fire in her forests, and it will devour everything around her.
Thus says the Lord: Go down to the house of the king of Judah, and speak this word there,
and say: Hear the word of the Lord, king of Judah, you who sit on the throne of David, you and your house and your servants and your people, and those who enter through these gates.

Thus says the Lord: Do judgment and righteousness, and rescue the one who has been robbed from the hand of the one who wrongs him. Do not oppress the stranger, the orphan, or the widow; do not become ungodly; and do not shed innocent blood in this place.
For if you really do this word, then kings who sit on the thrones of David will enter through the gates of this house, riding on chariots and horses, they and their servants and their people.
If you do not do these words, I swear by myself, says the Lord, that this house will become a desolation.
For thus says the Lord concerning the house of the king of Judah: Gilead, you are to me the head [?] of Lebanon; yet I will surely make you a desert, cities that are desolate and uninhabited.
And I will send against you a destroying man with an axe in his hands, and they will cut down all your choice firs and throw them into the fire.
And the nations will pass through this city, and each one will say to his neighbour, “Why has the Lord done this to such a great city?”
And they will say, “Because they abandoned the law of the Lord their God, and worshipped foreign gods and served them.”
Do not weep for the one who has died. Weep bitterly for the one who is going away, for he will never come back again or see this land, his own country.
For thus says the Lord concerning Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah, who reigned in place of his father Josiah, and who went out from this place: he will never come back here again.
For in the place where they have carried him captive, there he will die, and he will not see this land again.
Woe to him who builds his house without righteousness and his upper rooms without justice, who makes his neighbour work for nothing and does not give him his wages.
You have built yourself a house [?], with spacious upper rooms fitted with windows, panelled with cedar and painted with vermilion.
But will you reign because you compete angrily with the cedar? Did your father not eat and drink, and also do justice and righteousness?
Then it was well with him. He judged the cause of the lowly and the fallen, and it was well with him. Or is this not what it means to know me? says the Lord.
Look, neither your eyes nor your heart are good. They are set only on your greed, on shedding innocent blood, on slander, and on committing murder and harm.

Therefore this is what the Lord says about Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: Woe to that man! They will not lament him with "Woe, brother," nor weep for him with "Woe is me, lord" and "Woe is me, brother."
He will be buried as a donkey is buried; [?] he will be thrown out beyond the gates of Jerusalem.
Go up to Lebanon and cry out, raise your voice as far as Bashan, and shout across the sea, for all your lovers have been crushed.
I spoke to you in your straying, and you said, "I will not listen." This has been your way since your youth: you did not listen to my voice.
The wind will shepherd all your shepherds, and your lovers will go into captivity. Then you will be ashamed and disgraced by all who love you,
you who live in Lebanon and nest among the cedars. You will groan when pains come upon you like those of a woman giving birth.
As I live, says the Lord, even if Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were the signet ring on my right hand, [?] I would tear you off from there.
I will hand you over to those who seek your life, whom you fear to face: to Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and to the Chaldeans.
I will throw you and the mother who bore you out into another land, a land where you were not born, and there you will die.
They will never return to the land that they long with all their soul to return to.
That face is despised, and this man is cast out. Jeconiah has been despised like a useless vessel, for he and his descendants were cast out and thrown into a land that he did not know.
O land, land, land, hear the word of the Lord!

This is what the Lord says: Record this man as a man cast out, a man who will not prosper in his days. For no man from his descendants will ever again rise to sit on the throne of David as ruler of Judah.
O shepherds, you who scatter and destroy the sheep of my pasture, says the Lord!

Therefore this is what the Lord, the God of Israel, says about the shepherds of my people: You have scattered my sheep, driven them away and neglected them. So I will take vengeance on you for the wickedness of your ways, says the Lord.
I will gather the remnant of my people from all the lands where I have driven them, and I will bring them back to their pasture, and they will grow and multiply.
I will set shepherds over them who will tend them, and they will no longer be afraid or terrified, says the Lord.
The days are coming, says the Lord, when I will raise up for David a righteous Rising, and a righteous king will reign. He will understand, and he will do justice and righteousness on the earth.
In his days Judah shall be saved, and Israel shall dwell in hope. And this is their name which the Lord shall give them: Josedek. Among the prophets.

Therefore, behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when they shall no longer say, "The Lord lives, who brought the sons of Israel up out of the land of Egypt." Therefore, behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when they shall no longer say, "The Lord lives, who brought the sons of Israel up out of the land of Egypt,"

but rather, "The Lord lives, who brought up and led the offspring of the house of Israel out of the land of the north and out of all the lands where I had scattered them." And I will [?] them again, and they shall dwell in their own land. But rather, "The Lord lives, who brought up and gathered all the offspring of Israel out of the land of the north and out of all the lands where he had driven them away"; and he [?] them again in their own land.

Concerning the prophets. My heart is broken within me, and all my bones are shaken. I have become like a broken man, and like a man overcome by wine, because of the Lord and because of the beauty of his glory.
For the land is filled with adultery, and because of them the land has mourned. The pastures of the wilderness have dried up; their course has become evil and their strength is nothing.
For the priests and the prophets have defiled themselves, and in my house I have seen their wickedness, said the Lord.
Therefore let their way become for them a slippery place in the mist, and let them stumble and fall in it, for I will bring evil upon them in the year of their visitation.
And among the prophets of Samaria I have seen lawless deeds: they prophesied in my name by Baal, and led my people Israel astray.

And among the prophets of Jerusalem I have seen a horrible thing: they committed adultery and walked in falsehood, and strengthened the hands of the wicked, so that no one turned back from his evil way. They have all become to me like Sodom, and its inhabitants like Gomorrah.

Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts concerning the prophets: Behold, I will feed them with pain and give them bitter water to drink, for from the prophets of Jerusalem defilement has gone out into all the land.
Thus says the Lord Almighty: Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy vanity. They speak the vision of their own evil heart, and not from the mouth of the Lord.

They say to those who turn away from the words of the Lord, "Peace shall be with you"; and to all who walk in their own wills, all who walk in the error of their own heart, they said, "No evil shall come upon you." [?]
For who has stood in the council of the Lord and seen his word? Or who has drawn near, and his ears have heard?
Behold, a shaking from the Lord, and wrath goes forth to shake; it shall come all at once upon the ungodly.
And the wrath of the Lord shall not turn back until he has acted and until he has carried out all the purposes of his heart. At the end of days they shall understand them.
I did not send the prophets, yet they ran; I did not speak to them, yet they prophesied.
And if they had stood in my council and heard my words, they would have taught my people and turned them back from their evil way and from the wickedness of their conduct,
I am a God who is near, says the Lord, and not a God who is far off.
Can a man hide himself in a hiding place so that I do not see him? said the Lord. Do I not fill heaven and earth? said the Lord.
I have heard what the prophets say, who prophesy falsely in my name and say, "I have seen a vision."
How long will this be in the heart of the prophets who prophesy falsehood, and who prophesy the desire of their own heart,
who plan to make my people forget my law through their visions, which each one tells to his neighbour, just as their fathers forgot my name because of Baal?
Let the prophet who has a vision tell his vision; and let the one who has my word speak my word truthfully. What is chaff compared with wheat? So too are my words, said the Lord.
Behold, my words are like a blazing fire, says the Lord, and like a hammer that splits the rock.
Behold, I am against the prophets, says the Lord, who steal my words, each one from his neighbour.
Behold, I am against the prophets, said the Lord, who bring out prophecies of the tongue, and with lies make [?], and sleep their sleep.

Behold, I am against the prophets who prophesied false visions, said the Lord, and told them, and led my people astray with their lies and their falsehoods. I did not send them, nor did I command them, and they will bring no benefit to this people, said the Lord.
And if the people, or a priest, or a prophet asks you, "What is the oracle of the Lord?" then say to them: "You are the oracle of the Lord, and I will cast you off, said the Lord."
As for the prophet and the priest and the people who say this "oracle of the Lord," I will take vengeance on that man and on his house.
For this is what each one should say to his neighbour, and each one to his brother: "What has the Lord answered you?" and "What has the Lord said?"
And do not use the name "oracle of the Lord," for each man's own word will become an oracle of the Lord to him, and you have perverted the words of the living God, of the Lord of hosts, our God.
This is what you shall say to the prophets: "What has the Lord answered you?" and "What has the Lord said to you?" But do not say "oracle of the Lord."
Therefore the Lord says this: Because you have said this word, "oracle of the Lord," even though I sent to you and said, "Do not say 'oracle of the Lord,'"
therefore, behold, I will take you up as an oracle and cast you off, you and the city that I gave to you and to your fathers, away from my presence.
And I will bring upon you everlasting reproach and everlasting disgrace, which will not be forgotten.

The Lord showed me two baskets of figs set in front of the temple of the Lord. This was after Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, had carried away into captivity Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, together with the princes of Judah, the craftsmen, the offerers, and the rich. He carried them away captive from Jerusalem and brought them to Babylon.
One basket had very sweet figs, like ripe early figs, and the other basket had very bad figs, which could not be eaten because they were so bitter.
And the Lord said to me, "What do you see, Jeremiah?" And I said, "Figs: very sweet figs, and very bad figs that cannot be eaten because they are so bad."
And the word of the Lord came to me, and he said to me:
Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Like these good figs, so I will regard the exiles of Judah, whom I sent away from this place to the land of the Chaldeans, for good.
And I will set my eyes upon them for good, and I will bring them back to this land. I will build them up and not tear them down; I will plant them and not uproot them.
And I will give them a heart to know me, that I am the Lord. They shall be my people and I will be their God, for they shall return to me with their whole heart.

And like the bad figs, which cannot be eaten because they are so bad, thus says the Lord, so I will give up Zedekiah king of Judah, and his wealthy men, and the remnant of Jerusalem who are left in this land, and those who live in Egypt.
And I will give them up to be scattered among all the kingdoms of the earth, to be a reproach, a byword, a thing hated and a curse in every place where I drive them.
And I will send famine, death and the sword upon them, until they are wiped out from the land that I gave to them and to their fathers.
The word that came to Jeremiah concerning all the people of Judah in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, which was the first year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon.
The word which Jeremiah the prophet spoke to all the people of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and he said:

From the thirteenth year of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah, until this day, for twenty-three years, the word of the Lord has come to me, and I have spoken to you. I rose early and spoke to you, and you did not listen.
And I sent to you my servants the prophets; I sent them early in the morning, and you did not listen, and your ear did not [?] to hear my words.
And I said: Turn back, each of you, from your evil way and from your wicked conduct, and dwell in the land that I gave to you and to your fathers from of old and for ever.
And do not follow after foreign gods to serve them and to worship them, so that you do not provoke me to anger by the works of your hands and bring harm on yourselves.
But you did not listen to me, says the Lord, so that you provoked me to anger by the works of your hands, to your own [?].
Therefore thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Because you did not believe my words,

behold, I will send and bring all the tribes of the north, says the Lord, and Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and I will bring them against this land and against its inhabitants and against all the nations around it. I will lay them waste and make them a ruin, a thing to hiss at, and a reproach for ever.
And I will take away from them the sound of mirth and the sound of joy, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the grinding of flour and the light of the lamp.
And the whole land shall become a ruin and a desolation, and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon among the Gentiles for seventy years.

And when the seventy years are completed, I will take vengeance on the king of Babylon, and I will punish that nation, says the Lord, for their iniquities, and the land of the Chaldeans, and I will make it a ruin for ever.
And I will bring upon this land all my words that I have spoken against it, everything written in this book,
which Jeremiah prophesied against all the nations. For many nations and great kings will enslave them. And I will repay them according to their deeds, and according to the wickedness of their ways.
For thus the Lord, the God of Israel, said to me: “Take this cup of unmixed wine from my hand, and make all the nations to whom I send you drink it.”
“And they shall drink, and vomit, and go mad because of the sword that I will send among them.”
And I took the cup from the hand of the Lord, and made all the nations to whom the Lord had sent me drink it:
Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, and its kings and its princes, to make them a desolation, a trackless waste, an object of hissing, and a curse;
and Pharaoh king of Egypt, and his servants, and his nobles,

and all his people, and all the mixed peoples among them, and all the kings of the region, and all Arabia, and all the kings of the land of Uz, and all the kings of the land of the foreigners: Ashkelon, and Gaza, and Ekron, and the remnant of Ashdod;
and Edom, and Moab, and the sons of Ammon;
and all the kings of Tyre, and all the kings of Sidon, and all the kings of the regions that are beyond the sea;
and Dedan, and Tema, and Buz,
and all who are shaven at the front of the face [?], and all the kings of Arabia, and all the kings of the mixed peoples who dwell in the desert, and all the kings of Zimri;
and all the kings of Elam, and all the kings of the Arsacids, and of the Persians;
and all the kings of the east, far and near, each one with his brother, and all the kingdoms of the earth that are on the face of the earth; and King Sheshach shall drink after them.
And say to them: “Thus says the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel: Drink, and be drunk, and vomit, and fall, and rise no more, because of the sword that I will send among you.”
And if they refuse to take the cup from your hand to drink it, say to them: “Thus said the Lord of hosts: You shall surely drink.

For behold, I begin to bring evil on the city that is called by my name; and will you be cleansed? You will by no means be cleansed, for I am calling down a sword upon all who dwell on the earth, said the Lord of hosts.”

And you shall prophesy all these words to them, and say to them: “The Lord commands from on high, and from his holy place he will utter his voice, and he speaks his word from his dwelling place; and they shall answer like those who tread grapes. Destruction is coming upon all who dwell on the earth,
upon a part of the earth, for the Lord has a judgment against the nations; he will judge all flesh, and the ungodly will be given over to the sword,” said the Lord.
Thus says the Lord of hosts: “Behold, evil is going forth from nation to nation, and a great whirlwind is going out from the end of the earth.”

And those struck down by the Lord on that day of the Lord shall lie from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth. They shall not be mourned, nor gathered, nor buried; they shall be as dung on the face of the earth.
Cry out, shepherds, and raise your voice; lament, rams of the flock, for the days of your slaughter and your scattering are fulfilled, and you will fall like choice rams.
There will be no flight left for the shepherds, and no escape for the rams of the flock.
Hear the shepherds crying out and the rams of the flock wailing, for the Lord has destroyed their pasture.
And the good things of peace have fallen before the fury of the Lord's anger.
Each one has left his dwelling, like a lion, for their land has become a land without paths before the fury, before the great sword, and before the fury of his anger.
At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came from the Lord, and he said:

Thus the Lord said to me: Stand in the court of the house of the Lord, and speak to all of Judah who come to worship in the house of the Lord. Tell them all the words that I have commanded you to tell them; do not hold back a word.
Who knows? Perhaps they will listen, and each one will turn from his evil way, and I will relent from the evil that I have planned to do to them because of their wicked ways.
And say to them: Thus says the Lord: If you do not listen to me and walk in my law, which I set before you,
and listen to the words of my servants the prophets, whom I sent to you early, and you did not listen,
then I will make this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse for all the nations of the earth.
And the priests, the false prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the house of the Lord.

And when Jeremiah had finished speaking all that the Lord had commanded him to tell all the people, the priests, the false prophets, and all the people seized him and said to him, "You shall surely die,

because you prophesy in the name of the Lord and say, 'This house will be like Shiloh, and this city will be emptied of its inhabitants.'" And all the people gathered around Jeremiah in the house of the Lord.
When the princes of Judah heard these words, they came up from the king's palace to the house of the Lord and sat at the doors of the New Gate of the Lord's house.

And the priests and the false prophets said to the princes and to all the people, "This man deserves the sentence of death, because he has prophesied against this city, as you have heard with your own ears."
And Jeremiah said to the princes and to all the people, "The Lord sent me to prophesy against this house and this city all these words that you have heard.
Now therefore amend your ways and your deeds, and listen to the voice of the Lord your God, and the Lord will relent from the evils that he has pronounced against you.
As for me, I am in your hands; do with me as is right and as seems best to you.

But know for certain that if you kill me, you will bring innocent blood upon yourselves, upon this city, and upon those who live in it, for truly the Lord sent me to you to speak all these words in your hearing."
Then the princes and all the people said to the priests and the false prophets, "This man does not deserve the sentence of death, for he has spoken to us in the name of the Lord our God."
And some of the elders of the people stood up and spoke to the whole assembly of the people, saying:

"Micah the Moreshethite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and he said to all the people of Judah: 'Thus says the Lord: Zion shall be ploughed like a field, and Jerusalem shall become like a hut for guarding fruit, and the mountain of the house of the Lord shall become a wooded thicket.'

Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? No, they feared the Lord and pleaded before the face of the Lord, and the Lord relented from the evils he had spoken against them. And we are doing great evil against our own souls."

And there was a certain man who prophesied in the name of the Lord: Uriah son of Shemaiah, of Kiriath-jearim. He prophesied against this city and concerning this land, just as in all the words of Jeremiah.
And King Jehoiakim, all his wealthy men and all the princes heard all his words, and they sought to kill him. Uriah heard of it and was afraid, and he fled and went into Egypt.
And King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt, Elnathan son of Achbor and men with him.
And they brought him out from there and brought him to King Jehoiakim, who killed him with the sword and threw his corpse into the burial place of the common people.
But the hand of Ahikam son of Shaphan was with Jeremiah, so that he was not handed over to the people to be killed.
At the beginning of the reign of King Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came to Jeremiah from the Lord, and he said:
Thus the Lord said to me: "Make yourself bonds and yoke-bars, and put them on your neck.
And send them to the king of Judah, the king of the Ammonites, the king of Tyre and the king of Sidon, by the hand of the envoys who are coming to Jerusalem to meet Zedekiah king of Judah.
And give them a command for their lords, and say: 'Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

Thus shall you say to your lords: I made the earth, and humankind, and the animals, as many as are on the face of the earth, by my great power and by my uplifted arm; and I have given it to whomever I please. And now I myself
will give all this land into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, my servant, and the wild animals of the field also to serve him.
All the nations shall be given over to him to serve him, and his son, and his son's son, until the time of his wrath comes. Many nations and great kings shall serve him.

And if any nation or kingdom will not serve Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and will not put its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon, I will punish them with sword, famine and death, says the Lord, until they are wiped out by his hand.
So do not listen to your false prophets, your diviners, your visions, your soothsayers, your augurs and your sorcerers, who tell you: "Do not serve the king of Babylon."
For they prophesy a lie to you, in order to remove you far from your land. I will scatter you, and you will perish.
But the nation that puts its neck under the yoke of the king of Babylon and serves him, I will leave on its land, says the Lord, and it shall till it and live there.'"
And I spoke to Zedekiah, king of Judah, in the same way, with all these words, and I said: Bring your necks under the yoke of the king of Babylon, and serve him and his people, and you will live.
Why should you and your people die by the sword, by famine and by pestilence, as the Lord has spoken concerning the nation that will not serve the king of Babylon?
Do not listen to the words of the false prophets who tell you, 'Do not serve the king of Babylon,' for they prophesy falsehood to you.
For I did not send them, says the Lord, and they prophesy to you falsely in my name, so that they may destroy you, and you will perish, and those prophets with you.

And I spoke to the priests and to all the people, and said: Thus says the Lord: Do not listen to the words of the prophets who prophesy to you and say, 'Behold, the vessels of the house of the Lord will now soon be brought back from Babylon,' for they prophesy falsehood to you. I did not send them, and the word of the Lord is not among them.
Do not listen to them; serve the king of Babylon, and you will live. Why should this city become a desolation?

If they are prophets, and the word of the Lord is among them, let them plead with the Lord of hosts, so that the remaining vessels of the house of the Lord, and of the house of the king of Judah, and of Jerusalem, may not be carried off to Babylon.
For thus says the Lord of hosts concerning the pillars, and concerning the sea, and concerning the stands, and concerning the rest of the vessels that are left in this city,
which Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, did not take away when he carried Jeconiah and Joakim, kings of Judah, captive from Jerusalem to Babylon, together with all the nobles of Judah and Jerusalem.
For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, concerning the vessels that are left in the house of the Lord, and in the house of the king of Judah, and in Jerusalem:
They will be carried to Babylon, and there they will remain until the day of their visitation, says the Lord; and then I will bring them up and return them to this same place.

And it came to pass in that year, at the beginning of the reign of Zedekiah, king of Judah, in the fourth year, in the fifth month, that Hananiah son of Azzur, the false prophet from Gibeon, spoke in the house of the Lord before the eyes of the priests and of all the people, and said:
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Within two years' time I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon,
and I will bring back to this place all the vessels of the house of the Lord, which Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, took away from this place and carried to Babylon.

And Jeconiah son of Joakim, king of Judah, and all the captives of Judah who went to Babylon, I will bring back to this same place, so the Lord has said, together with the exiles of Judah; for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.
And Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Hananiah the false prophet before the eyes of the priests and before the eyes of all the people who were standing in the house of the Lord;

and Jeremiah the prophet said: Truly, may the Lord do so, and may the Lord confirm this word of yours which you prophesy, that the vessels of the house of the Lord and all the captives will be brought back from Babylon to this same place.
But hear this word, which I speak in your ears and in the ears of all the people.
The prophets who were before me and before you from of old prophesied concerning many lands and concerning great kingdoms: of war, of evil, and of death.
And as for the prophet who prophesied peace: when the word of that prophet comes to pass, then that prophet will be known as one whom the Lord truly sent to them.
Then Hananiah the false prophet took the yoke-bars from the neck of Jeremiah the prophet before the eyes of all the people and broke them.

And Hananiah spoke before the eyes of all the people and said, "Thus says the Lord: In this way I will break the yoke of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, from the neck of all the nations within two years' time." And Jeremiah the prophet went his way.
And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah after Hananiah the false prophet had broken the yoke-bars from his neck, and said:
"Go and speak to Hananiah and say to him, 'Thus says the Lord: You have broken the wooden yoke-bars, and in their place I will make yoke-bars of iron.'

For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: I have put a yoke of iron on the neck of all the nations, so that they may serve Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and be his slaves; and I have given him even the beasts of the field."
And Jeremiah the prophet said to Hananiah the false prophet, "Listen, Hananiah: the Lord has not sent you, and you have made this people trust in a lie.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I am sending you away from the face of the earth. This year you will die, because you have spoken rebellion against the Lord."
And Hananiah the false prophet died that same year, in the seventh month.

And these are the words of the letter that Jeremiah the prophet sent from Jerusalem to the elders of the captives, and to the priests, the false prophets, and to all the people: a letter to Babylon, to the captives and to all the people whom Nebuchadnezzar had carried away captive from Jerusalem to Babylon.
This was after King Jeconiah, the queen, the eunuchs, and the princes of Judah had gone out from Jerusalem, along with every nobleman, craftsman, and prisoner from Jerusalem.
It was sent by the hand of Elasah son of Shaphan and Gemariah son of Hilkiah, whom Zedekiah king of Judah sent to Babylon, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. And it said:
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, concerning the captives whom he carried away captive from Jerusalem to Babylon:
Build houses and live in them; plant gardens and eat their fruit.
Take wives and have children, sons and daughters. Take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands, and let them bear sons and daughters; multiply there, and do not decrease.
And live in the peace of the land to which I have sent you, and pray to the Lord for its people, for in their peace you too will have peace.

For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Do not let your false prophets who are among you deceive you, and do not let your diviners deceive you, and do not listen to your dreams that you dream.
For they prophesy lies to you in my name; I did not send them, says the Lord.
For thus says the Lord: When you complete seventy years in Babylon, I will visit you, and I will establish my good words upon you, to [?] (bring you back) to this place.

For I know the plan, for it is I, and I will plan for you a plan of peace, says the Lord, and not of evil, to give you these very great things and hope; and you shall call upon me, and you shall find me.
And you shall pray to me, and I will hear you;
you shall seek me and you shall find me, when you seek me with all your heart.

And I will appear to you, says the Lord, and I will turn back your captivity, and I will gather you from all the nations and from all the places where I have scattered you, says the Lord. And I will bring you back to this place, from which I carried you away captive.
For thus says the Lord to the king who sits on the throne of David, and to all the people, the inhabitants of this land, your brothers who did not go out with you into captivity:
Thus says the Lord of hosts: Behold, I will send upon them the sword and famine and death, and I will make them like suarim [?] (vile) figs, which cannot be eaten because of their badness [?].

And I will pursue them with the sword and famine and death, and I will give them up to be a reproach to all the kings of the earth, and a curse and a ruin and a hissing, and a reproach among all the nations where I have scattered them.
Because they did not listen to my words, says the Lord, for I sent to them my servants the prophets, rising early and sending them, and they did not listen, says the Lord.
And you, hear the word of the Lord, all you captives whom I sent away from Jerusalem to Babylon.
And you said: The Lord has raised up a prophet for us in Babylon.

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, concerning Ahab son of Kolaiah and concerning Zedekiah son of Manasseh, who prophesy lies in my name: Behold, I will deliver them into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he will slay them before your eyes.

And a curse will be taken up from them among all the captives of Judah in Babylon, and they will say: May the Lord do to you as he did to Zedekiah and to Ahab, whom the king of Babylon roasted in the fire.

For they committed lawlessness in Israel, and they committed adultery with the wives of their fellow citizens, and spoke words falsely in my name, which I did not command them; and I am the one who knows and am witness, says the Lord.
And to Shemaiah the Elamite say:
Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: For you sent a letter in my name to all the people in Jerusalem. I did not send you in my name; and to Zephaniah son of Manasseh [you wrote]:

'The Lord has appointed you priest in place of the priest Judah [?] (Jehoiada), and made you overseer in the house of the Lord over every man who prophesies and every crafty man, that you should put them in the prison of the stocks [?] (sinuk) and in the pit.'
'And now why have you not been angry with Jeremiah of Anathoth, who prophesied to you?'
'For he sent to you in Babylon and said to you: It is far off [?]; build houses and dwell in them, plant gardens and eat their fruit.'
And Zephaniah the priest read this letter aloud in the hearing of Jeremiah the prophet.
And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, and said to him,
"Send to all the captives and say: Thus says the Lord concerning Shemaiah the Elamite: Because Shemaiah has prophesied to you, and I did not send him, and he has made you trust in a lie,

therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will punish Shemaiah the Elamite and his descendants. He shall have no man sitting among you to see the good that I will do for you, says the Lord, because he spoke perversion against the Lord."
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, and he said:
"Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Write for yourself in a book all these words that I have commanded you.

For behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will bring back the captivity of my people Israel and Judah, said the Lord. I will bring them back to this place, which I gave to their fathers, and they shall possess it."
And these are the words that the Lord spoke concerning Israel and concerning Judah.
Thus said the Lord of hosts: "You have heard a sound of fear, a terrible fear, and there is no peace.

Ask and see whether a [?] has given birth to a child, and concerning the fear by which loins and deliverance [?] were seized. For I have seen every man with his hands on his loins like a woman in labor. All faces have turned and become pale.
For that day is great, and there is none [?] like it. It is a time of distress and of affliction for Jacob.
And from this too they shall be saved [?]. On that day, said the Lord of hosts, I will break the yoke from their neck and burst their bonds, and they shall no longer serve foreigners.
They shall serve the Lord their God, and I will raise up David as king for them.

And you, my servant Jacob, do not be afraid, said the Lord, and do not tremble, Israel. For behold, I will save you from afar, and your descendants from their captivity. Jacob shall return and be at rest and be at ease, and there shall be no one to frighten them.

For I am with you, says the Lord, to save you. For I will make an end of all the nations among whom I have scattered you, but of you I will not make an end. I will discipline you with judgment, but I will not leave you wholly unpunished."
Thus says the Lord: "Your breaking is severe; your wound is painful.
There is no one to plead your cause. You were treated painfully [?], and there is no help for you.

All your friends have forgotten you; they do not ask after you. For I have struck you with the wound of an enemy, a harsh discipline, for all your iniquity, because your sins have multiplied. Your iniquities have overpowered you.
Why do you cry out over your breaking? Your pain is severe because of the multitude of your iniquities, for your sins have overpowered you and have done this to you.

Therefore all who devour you shall be devoured, and all your enemies shall eat all their own flesh [?]. Through the multitude of your iniquities they multiplied, and your sins have done this to you. All who afflict you shall go into captivity. Those who pursue you shall become the pursued [?], and I will give all who took you captive into captivity.
"For I will bring you healing from your painful wounds, and I will heal you," says the Lord, "because you were called 'Scattered', Zion: 'This is your prey, for there is no one who seeks after her.'"

Thus says the Lord: "Behold, I will bring back the uprooted ones of the dwellings of Jacob, and I will have mercy on his captives. The city shall be built on its height, and the temple shall be set up according to its right order."
"And from them shall come forth [?] and the voice of singers. I will multiply them, and they shall not decrease; I will increase them, and they shall not be diminished."
"Their sons shall go in as at first, and their testimonies shall be established before my face, and I will take vengeance on all who oppress them."

"Their mighty ones shall be over them, and their ruler shall come forth from among them. I will gather them, and they shall return to me. For who is this who would have turned his heart to me?" says the Lord.
"And they shall be my people, and I will be their God."
For the wrath of the Lord has gone forth in anger; wrath has gone forth, whirling about; it shall come upon the ungodly.
The wrath of the Lord's anger shall not turn back until he has acted and until he has carried out the will of his heart. In the last days you shall understand this.
"At that time," said the Lord, "I will be God to the race of Israel, and they shall be my people."
Thus said the Lord: "I found uprightness in the wilderness among those who destroy with the sword, who went to torment Israel. Let us go, and do not destroy Israel."
From afar the Lord shall appear to them: "I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have drawn you to mercy."
"For I will build you up, and you shall be built, virgin Israel. Again you shall take up your timbrel and go out with the companies of singers."
"Again you shall plant vineyards on the mountain of Samaria. Plant the planting and give praise."
"For it is a day of comfort for those who make supplication on the mountains of Ephraim: 'Arise, and let us go up to Zion, to the Lord our God.'"
For thus the Lord says to Jacob: "Rejoice and be glad, and sing over the heads of the nations. Make it heard, give praise, and say: 'The Lord has saved his people, the remnant of Israel.'"

"Behold, I will bring them from the land of the north and gather them from the end of the earth at the feast of Passover. And many peoples shall be born to you [?], among them the lame and the blind, the pregnant woman and the woman in labor, together a great assembly, and they shall return here."

"With weeping they went out from you, and with comfort I will bring them back. I will give them rest by streams of water on a straight road, and they shall no longer go astray on it, for I have become a father to Israel, and Ephraim is my firstborn."
Hear the word of the Lord, you nations, and declare it to the distant coastlands. Say: "He who scattered Israel will gather him and will keep him as a shepherd keeps his flock."
For the Lord has redeemed Jacob and delivered him from the hands of those stronger than he.

They shall come and rejoice and be glad on Mount Zion. They shall come and marvel at the good things of the Lord, at a land of wheat and wine and fruits, of flocks and cattle. Their soul shall be like a fruitful tree and like a well-watered garden, and they shall no longer be afraid, nor shall they hunger any more.

Then the virgins will rejoice in the assembly of young men, and the old men will be glad together. I will turn their mourning into joy, and I will comfort them and make them joyful, and I will gladden them out of their sorrow.
I will magnify and make drunk the soul of the priests, the sons of Levi, and my people will be filled with my good things, says the Lord.
Thus said the Lord: A voice was heard in Ramah, mourning, weeping and lamentation. Rachel was weeping for her children, and she would not be comforted for her children, because they are no more.
Thus says the Lord: Let your voice cease from weeping and your eyes from tears, for there is a reward for your works, said the Lord, and they will return from the land of the enemies.
And there will be hope for your end, said the Lord, and your children will return to their own borders.
I have surely heard the lamentation of Ephraim: You chastened me, and I was chastened; like an untamed calf I could not be tamed. Turn me back, and I will turn back, for you are the Lord my God.
For after my captivity I repented, and after I came to understanding I groaned over the days of my shame. I was put to shame and submitted to you, for I have borne reproach since my youth.

You are my beloved son, Ephraim, a child of delight in pleasure. For since my words are with him, I will surely remember him again. Therefore I sought him out; I will surely have mercy on him, says the Lord.

Set up watchmen for yourself, Zion; let there be bitter punishment for you. Set your heart toward your shoulders, toward the way by which you are going. Return, virgin Israel, return to your cities, you who mourn.
How long will you turn away, dishonoured daughter? For the Lord has created you for salvation and for planting anew; people will walk about in life.

Thus said the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Once again they will say this word in the land of Judah and in its cities, when I bring back their captives: Blessed is the Lord on his righteous, holy mountain.
And Judah and all its cities will dwell there together with those who work the land, and they will [?] with the flock.
For I have made every thirsty soul drunk, and I have filled every hungry soul with good things.
Because of this I woke up and looked, and my sleep was sweet to me.
Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will sow the house of Israel and the house of Judah with the seed of people and the seed of livestock.
And just as I kept watch over them to uproot and to tear down, to destroy, to do harm and to ruin, so I will keep watch over them to build up and to plant, says the Lord.
In those days they will no longer say: The fathers ate sour grapes, and the children's teeth were set on edge.
Instead, every person will die for their own sins, and whoever eats sour grapes, his own teeth will be set on edge.
Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make a covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah, a new covenant.

It will not be like the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt. For they did not hold to my covenants, and I disregarded them, said the Lord.

For this is the covenant that I have promised to the house of Israel and to the house of Judah after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws into their minds, and I will write them on their breasts, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.

And no longer shall each one teach his neighbor, and each one his brother, saying, "Know the Lord," for all of them shall know me, from the least of them to the greatest of them, says the Lord; I will remember [?].

Thus says the Lord, who gave the sun as light for the day, and the moon and the stars to give light to the night, and who gives a roar to the sea, and its waves [?]; the Lord [?] Almighty is his name.
If these laws cease from before my face, says the Lord, then the race of Israel shall also cease from being nations before my face all the days.
Thus says the Lord: If the heaven is raised up on high, and if the floor of the earth is lowered down below, then I too will reject the race of Israel, says the Lord, for all that they have done.
Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when the city of the Lord shall be built from the tower of Hananel to the corner gate.
And then hope [?] and the measuring line shall go out before them as far as the hills of Gareb, and it shall be made of choice stones toward Gabatha, and over all the valleys of Phagarim,

and all Asaremoth as far as the valley of firs [?], as far as the corner of the Horse Gate on the east, as a holy place of the Lord; and they shall no longer be uprooted, nor shall they be destroyed forever.
The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah, a prophecy: in the tenth year of Zedekiah, king of Judah, which was the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon,
when the army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem, and they were keeping Jeremiah the prophet under guard in the court of the prison, which is in the porticoes of the king of Judah,

where Zedekiah, king of Judah, had confined him, and had said to him: "Why do you prophesy and say, 'Thus says the Lord: Behold, I am giving this city into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he shall seize it.'

'And Zedekiah, king of Judah, shall not escape from the hands of the Chaldeans, for he shall surely be given into the hands of the king of Babylon, and his mouth shall speak to his mouth, and his eyes shall see his eyes.'
'And he shall take Zedekiah to Babylon, and he shall stay there until I visit him, says the Lord; for he is fighting the Chaldeans, against whom he shall not prosper.'"
And Jeremiah the prophet said: The word of the Lord came to me, saying:

Behold, Hanamel, the son of Shallum, your father's brother, will come to you and say to you, "Buy that field of mine in Anathoth, for yours is the right of the next of kin to acquire it as an inheritance."

And Hanamel, the son of Shallum, my father's brother, came to me, as the Lord had said, in the court of the prison, and said to me: "Buy that field of mine in Anathoth, which is in the land of Benjamin, for it is your right to acquire the inheritance, because you are the eldest." And I understood that it was the word of the Lord.
And I bought the field from Hanamel, the son of Shallum, my father's brother, which was in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin, and I weighed out to him seven shekels of silver and ten pieces of silver.
And I wrote it in a deed, and had witnesses testify, and I weighed out the silver for him on the scales.
And I took the deed of purchase, the sealed one, with the terms and the ordinance, read out and made public.

And I gave the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, son of Maaseiah, before the eyes of Hanamel son of Shallum, my father's brother, before the eyes of the witnesses standing by and of the scribes of the deed of purchase, and before the eyes of all the Jews who were sitting in the court of the prison.
And I gave Baruch a command before their eyes, and said:

"Thus says the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel: Take this sealed deed of purchase, and the deed that was read out and made public, and put it in an earthenware vessel, so that it may last for many days."
"For thus said the Lord Almighty, the God of Israel: Houses and fields and vineyards will once again be bought in this land."
And after I had given the deed of purchase to Baruch son of Neriah, I prayed to the Lord and said:
"You who are Lord: behold, you made heaven and earth by your great power and your high arm, and nothing at all is hidden from you.
You show mercy to a thousand generations, and you repay the sin of the fathers into the bosom of their children after them.

O great and mighty God, Lord of hosts is your name. You are great in counsel and mighty in deed, Almighty, Lord of great name. Your eyes are open upon all the ways of the sons of men, to give to each according to his own way and according to the fruit of his doings.
You performed signs and wonders in the land of Egypt, and to this very day in Israel and among the offspring of men, and you made a name for yourself, as at this day.
And you brought your people Israel out of the land of Egypt with signs and wonders, with a strong hand and a high arm,
and with great sights. And you gave them this land, which you swore to their fathers to give them, a land flowing with milk and honey.

They went in and took possession of it, but they did not listen to your voice and did not walk in your law. All that you commanded them to do, they did not do, and so they caused all this evil to come upon them.

Behold, the people have come against this city to capture it, and the city has been given into the hands of the Chaldeans who are fighting against it, because of the sword, famine and death. As you said, so it is, and behold, you see it.

And you yourself, Lord, say to me: 'Buy the field with silver.' And I bought it, and wrote a deed and sealed it, and had witnesses testify, yet the city has been given into the hands of the Chaldeans."
And the word of the Lord came to me, and he said:
"I am the Lord, the God of all flesh. Will any word be hidden from me?
Therefore thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: This city will surely be given into the hands of the Chaldeans and into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and they will take it.

And the Chaldeans who are fighting against this city will come in and set it on fire and burn it. They will burn the houses on whose roofs they burned incense to Baal and offered sacrifices to other gods, so as to provoke me to bitterness.

For the children of Israel and the children of Judah have done nothing but evil before my eyes since their youth, and the children of Israel have provoked me to anger with the work of their hands, says the Lord.
For this city has been to me a cause of nothing but anger and wrath, from the day I built it until this day, and I will destroy it,

because of all the evil of the children of Israel and the children of Judah, for they embittered me: they and their kings, their priests, their prophets, the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.
They turned their backs to me and not their faces. I taught them; I rose early and taught them, but they did not listen and would not accept instruction.
They set their abominations in the house that is called by my name, to defile it with their uncleanness.

They built the high places of Baal in the valley of the son of Hinnom, in the towers in [?], to sacrifice their sons to Moloch, which I did not command them, nor did it come into my heart to do this abomination, to make Judah sin.
And now thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning this city, of which you say, "It is given into the hands of the king of Babylon by sword, by famine and by captivity":
Behold, I will gather them from all the places where I scattered them in my anger and my wrath and in great fury, and I will bring them back to this place and make them dwell in hope.
They will be my people, and I will be their God.
I will give them another heart and another way, so that they may fear me all their days, so that I may do good to them and to their children after them.
I will make with them an everlasting covenant, that I will not turn away from them, so that I may do them good; and I will put my fear in their hearts, so that they do not depart from me.
I will [?] them and rejoice over them, to do them good, and I will plant them in this land in truth, with all my heart and with all my soul.
For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Just as I brought all this great evil upon this people, so I will bring upon them all the good that I have promised them.
Fields will again be bought in this land, of which you say, "It is desolate, without man or beast; it is given into the hands of the Chaldeans."

Fields will be bought for silver, and deeds will be written in a book and sealed, and witnesses will be called, in the land of Benjamin, in the surroundings of Jerusalem, in the cities of Judah, in the cities of the hill country, in the cities of the Shephelah and in the cities of the Negeb; for I will bring back their captivity, says the Lord.
The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah a second time, while he was still bound in the court of the prison:
Thus says the Lord, who made the earth and formed it to establish it; the Lord is his name:
Call to me, and I will answer you, and I will tell you great and mighty things that you do not know.

For thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning the houses of this city and concerning the house of the king of Judah, which are to be pulled down for [?] and for defenses against the sword of the attackers,
to fight the Chaldeans and to fill them with the corpses of men, whom I will strike down in my wrath and my anger; I have turned my face away from them because of all their wickedness.
Behold, I will remove the sword from it, and behold, I will send [?] upon it. I will have mercy on them and heal them, and I will bring them peace and faithfulness.
And I will bring back the captives of Judah and the captives of Israel, and I will build them up as they were at first.

And I will cleanse them from all the iniquities by which they sinned against me. I will not remember the sins by which they sinned against me, and I will forgive the sins by which they turned away from me.

And it shall be for me a name of joy, of praise and of glory before all the nations of the earth that hear of all the good that I will do for them. They shall fear and marvel and be grieved because of all the good things and all the peace that I will do for them.

Thus said the Lord: Again there shall be heard in this place, of which you say, 'It is empty of people and of livestock,' in the cities of Judah and around Jerusalem, which are laid waste [?] and have no people or livestock,

the voice of joy, the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, and the voice of those who say: 'Give thanks to the Lord Almighty [?], for the Lord is good, for his mercy endures for ever.' And they shall offer praise [?] in the house of the Lord, for I will bring back the captives of this land as they were at first, said the Lord.

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: In this place, which is laid waste and has no people or livestock, and in all its cities, there shall again be a dwelling place for shepherds and for those who make their flocks lie down.

In the cities of the hill country and of the Shephelah, and in the cities of the Negeb, and in all the land of Benjamin, and around Jerusalem, and in the cities of Judah, flocks shall again pass under the hands of the one who counts them, said the Lord.
Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will fulfil the good word that I spoke concerning the house of Israel and concerning the house of Judah.
In those days and at that time I will raise up for David a righteous Branch, and he shall execute judgement and righteousness on the earth.
In those days Judea shall be saved and Jerusalem shall dwell in hope. And this is the name by which it shall be called: The Lord is our righteousness.
For thus says the Lord: David shall never lack a man to sit on the throne of the house of Israel.
And the Levitical priests shall never lack a man before my face to offer sacrifice, to burn incense, and to make offerings [?] all the days.
And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:
Thus says the Lord: If my covenant with the day and my covenant with the night could be broken, so that day and night did not come at their proper time,
then my covenant with David my servant could also be broken, so that he would have no son to reign on his throne, and my covenant with the priests and the Levites, my ministers.
Just as the host of heaven cannot be numbered and the sand of the sea cannot be counted, so I will multiply the descendants of David my servant and the Levites, my ministers.
And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:

Have you not seen what this people are saying? They have said, 'The two tribes that the Lord chose from among them, behold, he has cast them off [?].' And they have angered my people, so that it is no longer a nation before me.
Thus says the Lord: If I have not established [?] my covenant with day and night and the ordinances of heaven and earth,

Then I would also reject the descendants of Jacob and of David my servant, and not take from his descendants a ruler over the descendants of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. But I will bring back their captives and have mercy on them.

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, all his army, all the kingdoms under his rule and all the peoples were fighting against Jerusalem and against all the cities of Judah.
The Lord said: Go to Zedekiah king of Judah and tell him, 'This is what the Lord says: This city will certainly be handed over to the king of Babylon. He will capture it and burn it with fire.'
You will not escape from his hand. You will certainly be captured and handed over to him. You will see him eye to eye and he will speak to you face to face, and you will go to Babylon.
But hear the words of the Lord, Zedekiah king of Judah. This is what the Lord has said: You will not die by the sword.

You will die in peace. As people wept for your fathers, the kings who reigned before you, so they will weep for you too: 'Alas, lord!' They will mourn for you. For I have spoken great things [?], says the Lord.
Then the prophet Jeremiah told all these words to Zedekiah king of Judah in Jerusalem.

The army of the king of Babylon was fighting against Jerusalem and against the cities of Judah that were left [?], against Lachish and against Azekah. These were the only fortified cities left among the cities of Judah.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord after King Zedekiah made a covenant with the people in Jerusalem to proclaim release to them:
each person was to free his Hebrew male servant and his Hebrew female servant, so that no one would keep a fellow Israelite as a servant.

All the rich and all the people who had entered into the covenant listened and obeyed. Each was to free his male servant and his female servant and never enslave them again. They listened and set them free.
But after they had freed them, they changed their minds. They took back the male and female servants they had set free and made them servants and maidservants again.
Then the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, saying:
This is what the Lord, the God of Israel, has said: I made this covenant with your fathers on the day I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage:

'When six years are completed, you must free your Hebrew brother who has been sold to you. He will serve you for six years, and after the sixth year you must set him free from you.' But your fathers did not listen to me or pay attention to me.
Today you turned and did what is right in my eyes. Each of you proclaimed release to his neighbour, and you made a covenant before me in the house that is called by my name.

But then you turned back and profaned my name. Each of you [?] took back his male servant and his female servant whom you had set free to their own kin [?]. You forced them back into subjection to be your servants and maidservants.

Therefore thus says the Lord: You have not listened to me and proclaimed release, each to his brother and each to his neighbour. Behold, I proclaim to you, says the Lord, a release to the sword, to death and to famine, and I will give you over to be scattered among all the kings of the earth.
And I will give up the men who transgressed my covenant, which they made before my face: the calf which they cut in two, and they passed between its pieces.
The princes of Judah and the princes of Jerusalem, the rich and the priests and all the people of the land, who passed between the pieces of the calf.
I will give them into the hands of those who seek their life and into the hands of their enemies, and I will give their carcasses as food for the birds of the sky and the beasts of the earth.

And Zedekiah king of Judea and his princes I will give into the hands of their enemies, into the hands of those who seek their life, and into the hands of the army of the king of Babylon, who have withdrawn from them.

Behold, I will command them, says the Lord, and I will bring them back to this very city, and they will fight against it, take it and burn it with fire; and I will give the cities of Judah over to be laid waste, with no inhabitants.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord in the days of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, saying:
Go to the house of Rechab and call them, and bring them into the house of the Lord, into one of the courts, and give them wine to drink.
So I brought Jaazaniah son of Jeremiah, son of Habazziniah, and his brothers and his sons and the whole house of Rechab.

And I brought them into the house of the Lord, into the chamber of the sons of Hananiah son of Gedaliah, the man of God, which is near the chamber of the princes, above the chamber of Maaseiah son of Shallum, who kept the door.
And I set before the sons of Rechab jars full of wine, and cups, and I said to them: Drink wine.
But they said: We will not drink wine, for Jonadab son of Rechab, our father, commanded us, saying: You shall not drink wine, neither you nor your children, for ever;

you shall not build houses, nor sow seed, nor plant vineyards, nor shall you have any of these; but you shall dwell in tents all your days, so that you may live many days on the land in which you sojourn.
And we have obeyed the voice of Jonadab our father in everything that he commanded us: not to drink wine all our days, we, our wives, our sons and our daughters,
and not to build houses or settle in them; and we have had no vineyard, field or seed.
We have lived in tents, and we have obeyed and done everything that Jonadab our father commanded us.

But when Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came up against the land, we said: Come, let us go up and enter Jerusalem, away from the Chaldeans and from the army of the Assyrians; and so we settled in Jerusalem.
And the word of the Lord came to me, saying:
Thus said the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel:

Go and say to the men of Judah and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Will you still not receive instruction and listen to my words? says the Lord. The sons of Jonadab, son of Rechab, have kept the word that he commanded his children, not to drink wine, and they have not drunk it to this day, for they obeyed the commandment of their father. But I spoke to you; I rose early and spoke to you, and you did not listen to me.

And I sent to you my servants the prophets; I rose early and sent them, and I said to you: Turn back, every one of you, from his evil way, and make your ways better, and do not go after other gods to serve them, and you will dwell in the land which I gave to you and to your fathers. But you did not incline your ear, and you did not listen to me.
The sons of Jonadab, son of Rechab, have kept the commandment of their father which he commanded them, but this people has not listened to me.

Therefore thus said the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I am bringing upon Judah and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem all the evil that I spoke against them, because I spoke to them and they did not listen to me; I called to them and they did not answer me.

And say to the house of Rechab, Jeremiah: Therefore thus said the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Because the sons of Jonadab, son of Rechab, obeyed the commandment of Jonadab their father, and kept all his commandments, to do everything that their father commanded them,
therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: There shall never be lacking a man of the sons of Jonadab, son of Rechab, to stand before my face all the days of the earth.
And in the fourth year of Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah, the word of the Lord came to me and said to me:

Take for yourself the sheet of a book, and write on it all the words that I have commanded you concerning Israel and Jerusalem and Judah and all the nations, from the day I spoke to you, from the days of Josiah king of Judah, until this day.
Perhaps the house of Judah will hear all this evil that I intend to do to them, and they will turn, each one, from his evil way, and I will be merciful to their iniquities and their sins.
And Jeremiah called Baruch, son of Neriah, and Baruch wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah, on the sheet of the book, all the words of the Lord which he had commanded him.
And Jeremiah gave orders to Baruch and said to him: I am being guarded, and I am not able to enter the house of the Lord.

So go in and read aloud from this book which you have written from my mouth the words of the Lord, in the ears of the people in the house of the Lord on the days of fasting; and you shall read them aloud in the ears of all Judah who come from their cities.
Perhaps their prayer will be accepted before the Lord, and each one will turn from their evil way; for great is the anger and the wrath that the Lord has spoken against this people.
And Baruch, son of Neriah, spoke everything that Jeremiah the prophet had commanded him, reading aloud from the book the words of the Lord in the house of the Lord.
And in the fifth year of Jehoiakim, son of Josiah, king of Judah, in the ninth month, all Israel gathered to fast before the Lord, and all the people who came from the cities of Judah.

And Baruch read from the book the words of Jeremiah in the house of the Lord, in the chamber of Gemariah son of Shaphan the scribe, in the upper court, outside the new gates of the house of the Lord, in the hearing of all the people.
And Micaiah son of Gemariah son of Shaphan heard all the words of the Lord from the book.

And he went down to the king's house, to the assembly hall of the princes, the house of the scribe. All the princes were sitting there: Elishama the scribe, Delaiah son of Shemaiah, Elnathan son of Achbor, Gemariah son of Shaphan, Zedekiah son of Hananiah, and all the princes.
And Micaiah told them all the words that he had heard when Baruch read from the book in the hearing of the people.

And all the princes sent Jehudi son of Nethaniah son of Shelemiah son of Cushi to Baruch, and they said to him, "Take in your hand that book which you are reading in the hearing of the people, and come." So Baruch son of Neriah took the book in his own hand and went down to them.
And the princes said to Baruch, "Read it again in our hearing." And Baruch read it in their hearing.
And when all the princes had heard all those words, each one spoke to his neighbour. And they said to Baruch, "We must report all these words to the king."
And they questioned Baruch, saying, "Tell us, where did you write all these words from?"
And Baruch said, "From the mouth of Jeremiah. He was dictating all these words to me, and I was writing them in the book with ink."
And all the princes said to Baruch, "Go and hide, you and Jeremiah, and let no one know where you are."
And the princes went into the king's court. They gave the book to be kept in the house of Elishama the scribe, and they reported all these words to the king.
And the king sent Jehudi to fetch the book. Jehudi took it from the house of Elishama the scribe and read it in the hearing of the king and of all the princes who stood around the king.
And the king was sitting in the winter house in the ninth month, and braziers of fire stood before him.

And whenever Jehudi had read three or four columns, the king cut them off with the scribe's penknife and threw them into the fire that was on the braziers, until the whole book was used up in the fire of the braziers.
And the king and all his servants who heard these words did not seek the Lord, nor did they tear their garments.
Elnathan, Delaiah and Gemariah urged the king not to burn the book, but he did not listen to them.
And the king commanded Jerahmeel the king's son, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abiel to seize Baruch the scribe and Jeremiah the prophet. But they were hidden by the Lord.
And after the burning, when the king had burned the book in which were written all these words that Baruch had written from the mouth of Jeremiah, the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, and he said:
"Take another scroll, and write on it all the words that were in the scroll which Jehoiakim king of Judah burned."

And say to Jehoiakim, king of Judah: Thus says the Lord: You burned this book, and you said, '[?] did you write this book, [saying] that the king of Babylon will surely come in and destroy this land, and that man and beast will be cut off from it?'

For thus said the Lord concerning Jehoiakim, king of Judah: No one of his shall any longer sit on the throne of David, and his corpse shall be thrown out to the heat of the day and the frost of the night.

And I will punish him, and his offspring, and his servants for their iniquities; and I will bring upon them, and upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and upon the land of Judah all the evil that I spoke against them, because they did not listen to me.

And Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah, the scribe. And at Jeremiah's dictation Baruch wrote on it all the words of the book that King Jehoiakim had burned with fire, and many more words besides were added to them.
And Zedekiah son of King Josiah reigned in place of Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim; Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had made him king to reign over Judah.
And neither he, nor his servants, nor the people of the land listened to the words of the Lord which he spoke through Jeremiah the prophet.
And King Zedekiah sent Jehucal son of Shelemiah, and Zephaniah son of Maaseiah, the priest, to Jeremiah the prophet, and said: Pray for me to the Lord our God.
And Jeremiah was going in and out among the people, and they had not put him in prison.
And Pharaoh's army came out of Egypt, and the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard the report about them, and they withdrew from Jerusalem.
And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah the prophet, and said:

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Say this to the king of Judah, who sent you to me to inquire: Behold, Pharaoh's army, which has come out to help you, will turn back to their own land, to the land of Egypt;
and the Chaldeans will return; they will fight against this city, and take it, and burn it with fire.
Thus says the Lord: Do not deceive yourselves, saying, 'The Chaldeans will surely go away from us,' for they will not go away.

Even if you were to strike down the whole army of the Chaldeans who are fighting against you, and only some wounded men among them were left, each one in his tent, they would rise up and burn this city with fire.
And when the army of the Chaldeans withdrew from Jerusalem because of Pharaoh's army,
Jeremiah went out of Jerusalem to go to the land of Benjamin, to buy bread there among his people.

And he reached the Gate of Benjamin, and there was a man there with whom he used to lodge, Irijah son of Shelemiah, son of Hananiah. And he seized Jeremiah the prophet and said: You are deserting to the Chaldeans.
And Jeremiah said: That is a lie; I am not deserting to the Chaldeans. But he did not listen to him, and Irijah seized Jeremiah and brought him before the officials.

And the officials were angry with Jeremiah, and they beat him and put him in the prison house to be tormented, in the house of Jonathan the scribe, for his house had been made a prison. For the people [?] came to the house of the pit and to the [?];
and Jeremiah went into the house of the pit, the place of confinement, and stayed there many days.

And King Zedekiah sent and summoned Jeremiah, and the king questioned him secretly in his house and said to him, "Is there a word from the Lord?" And Jeremiah said, "There is: you will be handed over into the hands of the king of Babylon."
And Jeremiah the prophet said to King Zedekiah, "How have I sinned against you, or against your servants, or against this people, that you have put me in prison?
And where are your prophets who prophesied to you and told you, 'The king of Babylon will not come against you or against this land'?
And now hear me, I beg you, my lord king: let my plea for mercy come before you, so that you do not send me back to the house of Jonathan the scribe, so that I do not die there."

And King Zedekiah gave orders, and they put him in the prison house, and they gave him one loaf of bread a day from outside, where they make it, until the bread in the city ran out. And Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison.
And Zephaniah son of Nathan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jehoahaz son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchiah heard the words that Jeremiah was speaking to all the people,

for he said, "Thus says the Lord: Whoever stays in this city will die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence, but whoever goes out to the Chaldeans will live; his life will be spared to him as a prize.
For thus says the Lord: This city will surely be handed over into the hands of the army of the king of Babylon, and he will take it."

And the officials said to the king, "Let this man be put to death now, for he is weakening the hands of the fighting men who are left in the city, and he is weakening the hands of all the people by speaking such words to them. For this man does not speak for the good of this people, but tells them evil."
And King Zedekiah said, "Here he is; he is in your hands." For the king was not able to say anything against them.

And they seized Jeremiah and threw him into the cistern of Malchiah, the king's son, which was in the court of the prison, and they let him down into the pit with ropes. There was no water standing in the pit, only mire, and Jeremiah was in the mire.
And Ebed-melech the Ethiopian, a eunuch, who was in the king's house, heard that they had thrown Jeremiah into the cistern. And the king was sitting at the Gate of Benjamin.
And Ebed-melech went out to him, and Ebed-melech spoke to the king and said,

"My lord king, these men have done evil in all that they have done to Jeremiah the prophet, for they have thrown him into the cistern, and he will die there. You are doing evil, for you are handing the man of God over to death by famine, since there is no more bread in this city."
And the king gave orders to Ebed-melech the Ethiopian and said to him, "Take thirty men with you from here and bring him up out of the cistern, so that he does not die."

And Ebed-melech took the men and went into the house of the king, to the part beneath it, and took from there old rags and old ropes, and let them down to Jeremiah the prophet into the cistern; and he also brought woollen scraps.
And Ebed-melech the Ethiopian said to him, "Put these old rags and these woollen scraps under your armpits, beneath those ropes." And Jeremiah did so.
And they brought him up out of the cistern, and Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison.
And King Zedekiah sent and summoned him to his house of Asel, which was in the house of the Lord. And the king said to Jeremiah the prophet: "I will ask you something; do not hide anything from me."
And Jeremiah said to the king: "If I tell you, will you not surely put me to death? And if I give you counsel, you will not listen to me."
And King Zedekiah swore to him in secret and said: "As the Lord lives, who made this soul of ours, I will not kill you, and I will not give you into the hands of these men who seek your life."

And Jeremiah said to him: "Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: If you go out to the princes of the king of Babylon, your soul shall live, and this city shall not be burned with fire, and you and your house shall live.
If you do not go out to the princes of the king of Babylon, this city shall be given into the hands of the Chaldeans, and they shall burn it with fire, and you shall not escape from their hands."
And King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah: "I am concerned about the Jews who have gone over to the Chaldeans, that they may give me into their hands and they may mock me."
And Jeremiah said: "They will by no means give you up. Only listen to the words of the Lord that I speak to you, and it will be better for you, and your soul shall live.
But if you do not wish to go out, this is the word which the Lord has shown me:

Behold, all the women who were left in the house of the king of Judah were brought out to the princes of the king of Babylon, and they are saying: 'The men of your peace have deceived you and prevailed over you; they will overpower you when your foot slips [?], and they will turn away from you.'

And they will bring out all your wives and your children to the Chaldeans, and you will not escape from their hands, for you will be seized by the hand of the king of Babylon, and this city will be burned with fire."
And the king said to him: "Let no one know of these words, and you shall not die.

And if the princes hear that I have spoken with you, and they come to you and say to you, 'Tell us what the king said to you, and do not hide from us what you said to the king, and we will not kill you,'
then you shall say to them: 'I had come in to make supplication before the king, that he should not send me back again to the house of Jonathan to die there.'"
And all the princes came to Jeremiah and questioned him, and he told them all these words that the king had commanded him, and they left him in silence, for the word of the Lord had not been heard.
And Jeremiah remained in the court of the prison until the time Jerusalem was taken.

And it came to pass when Jerusalem was taken: in the ninth year of Zedekiah, king of Judah, in the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and all his army came against Jerusalem, and they fought against it.
And in the eleventh year of Zedekiah, in the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, they broke into the city.

And all the princes of the king of Babylon came in and sat in the middle gate: Nergal-sharezer, Samagad [?], and Nabusar, Sekkim Lapsaris [?], Nergal-sharezer and Rabamak, and all the other princes of the king of the Babylonians.

And when Zedekiah, king of Judah, and all the men of war saw them, they fled, and they went out of the city by night by the way of the royal garden, by the gate that was between the two walls, and they went out toward the way of the wilderness.

And the army of the Chaldeans pursued after them, and overtook Zedekiah in the plain of Jericho. They seized him and brought him before Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, to Riblah in the land of Hamath, and he passed judgment on him.
