And the king of Babylon slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah in Riblah before his eyes, and the king of Babylon slaughtered all the nobles of Judah.
And he put out the eyes of Zedekiah and bound him with fetters of bronze, so that they might take him to Babylon.
And the Chaldeans burned the houses of the king and the houses of the people with fire, and they tore down the wall of Jerusalem.
And the rest of the people who had remained in the city, and the deserters who had fallen into his hands,

and the remnant of the people who had escaped, Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard carried away captive to Babylon. But the poor of the people, who had nothing, Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard left in the land of Judah, and he gave them vineyards and irrigated land on that day.
And Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, gave command to Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard concerning Jeremiah, and said to him:
"Bring him, and set your eyes upon him, and do him no harm at all; but as he tells you, so do for him."
And Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard sent, together with Nebushazban [?] the Rabsaris, Nergal-sharezer the Rabmag, and all the great men of the king of Babylon,
and they called Jeremiah and brought him out of the court of the prison, and gave him to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, and they brought him out to [?], and he dwelt there among the people.
And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah while he was shut up and was in the court of the prison, and said:

"Go and say to Ebed-melech the Ethiopian: Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I am bringing my word upon this city for evil and not for good, and these things shall be before your face on this day, says the Lord.
And I will not give you into the hands of the men whose face you fear,
for I will surely deliver you, and you shall not fall by the sword, and your life shall be yours as a prize, because you trusted in me, says the Lord."

The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord after Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard had sent him away from Riblah, for he had taken him bound in manacles among all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah who were being carried away to Babylon.
And Nebuzaradan brought Jeremiah and said to him: "The Lord your God decreed this evil against this place and sent it upon this city;
and the Lord has done as he said, because they sinned against him, and you did not listen to his voice, and this thing has come upon you.
And now, behold, I have loosed you today from these manacles that were on your hands. If it seems good to you to come with me to Babylon, come, and I will set my eyes upon you."

And if it does not seem right in your eyes to come with me to Babylon, stay. Look, the whole land is before you. Wherever it is good and wherever it is right for you to go, go there [?]. And before I leave, go back to Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan, whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the land of Judah, and live with him among your people. If not, then go wherever seems good and pleasing to you; follow that. And the chief cook [?] gave him provisions and a gift, and sent him away.
And Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah, and lived with him among his people who had remained in the land.

And all the commanders of the forces who were in the countryside, they and their forces, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam over the land, and that he had entrusted to him their fathers and mothers and many of the poor people of the land, whom he had not carried away captive to Babylon.
And they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, and the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, they and their men.

And Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan swore an oath to them and said to them, "Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans. Live in this land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will be better for you.
And look, I will live in Mizpah to stand before the Chaldeans who come to you. As for you, gather wine, wheat and fruit, collect oil in your vessels, and live in your cities that you hold."

And all the Jews who were in the land of Moab, among the Ammonites and in Edom, and those who were in every land, heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judea and had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan over them. And the Jews returned from all the places where they had been scattered.
And they came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and they gathered wine and fruit in very great abundance.
And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces who were in the countryside came to Gedaliah at Mizpah.
And they said to Gedaliah, "Do you truly know that Baalis, king of the Ammonites, has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to you to kill you?" But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them.

And Johanan son of Kareah spoke to Gedaliah secretly in Mizpah and said to him, "Let me go now and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and let no one know of it. Otherwise he may somehow kill you, and all these Jews who have gathered to you will be scattered, and the remnant of Judah will perish."
And Gedaliah son of Ahikam said to Johanan son of Kareah, "Do not do this thing, for you are speaking falsely about Ishmael."

And in the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama, of the royal family, came with the king's servants and ten men to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah, and they ate bread with him there in Mizpah.

And Ishmael son of Nethaniah and the ten men who were with him rose up and struck Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan with the sword and killed him, the man whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
And Ishmael slaughtered all the Jews who were with Gedaliah in Mizpah, and all the Chaldeans who were found there, and the fighting men.
And on the second day after Ishmael had killed Gedaliah, when no one yet knew of it,

eighty men came from Shechem, from Salem and from Samaria, with their beards shaved, their garments torn, and mourning. They had offerings and incense in their hands to bring to the house of the Lord.
And Ishmael son of Nethaniah went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he walked. When he came near them, he said to them: "Come in to Gedaliah son of Ahikam."
And when they had come into the middle of the city, Ishmael and the men who were with him slaughtered them and threw them into the pit.
But ten men were found there who said to Ishmael: "Do not kill us, for we have stores of ours: barley, oil and honey." So he passed them by and did not kill them along with their brothers.

Now the pit into which Ishmael threw all the corpses of the men he had slain along with Gedaliah is a great pit, which King Asa made because of Baasha, king of Israel. Ishmael filled it with the slain.

And Ishmael carried off as captives all the people who were left in Mizpah, and the king's daughters, whom Nebuzaradan the [?] had entrusted to Gedaliah son of Ahikam. And Ishmael son of Nethaniah rose early and went over to the Ammonites.
And Johanan son of Kareah, and all the commanders of the forces who were with him, heard of all the evil that Ishmael son of Nethaniah had done.
And they gathered all their people, made ready for battle, and pursued Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and they found him by the great water at Gibeon.
And when all the people whom Ishmael was leading away saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces with him,
they rejoiced. And all the people whom Ishmael had taken captive from Mizpah turned back, and they returned and came to Johanan son of Kareah.
But Ishmael son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men and went to the Ammonites.

And Johanan son of Kareah, and all the commanders of the forces who were with him, took back the remnant of the people whom they had recovered from Ishmael son of Nethaniah after the killing of Gedaliah son of Ahikam, along with whom the mighty men had been slain in battle. They brought back from Gibeon this remnant, and the women and the eunuchs.
And they went and settled in the land of Geruth Chimham, which is near Bethlehem, intending to go on and go down to Egypt
because of the Chaldeans. For they were afraid of them, because Ishmael had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.
And all the commanders of the forces came: Johanan son of Kareah, Jezoriah son of Hananiah, and Azariah son of Joses, and all the people from the least to the greatest.

And they said to the prophet Jeremiah: "Let our plea for mercy come before you, and pray for us to the Lord your God for this remnant. For we who are left are few out of many, as your own eyes see us.
And may the Lord your God tell us the way in which we should walk and the thing that we should do."

And Jeremiah the prophet said to them: "I have heard. Behold, I will pray to the Lord my God according to your words. And whatever word the Lord says to me, I will tell you, and I will not hide a word from you."
And the leaders said to Jeremiah: "May the Lord be a true and faithful witness among us, that we will do according to every word with which the Lord your God sends you to us.
Whether it is good or whether it is evil, we will hear the voice of the Lord our God, to whom we are sending you, so that it may be better for us; for we will obey the voice of the Lord our God."
And after ten days, the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah.
And Jeremiah called Johanan son of Kareah, and the leaders of the forces who were with him, and all the people, from the least to the greatest,
and said to them: "Thus said the Lord, the God of Israel,

to whom you sent me to pour out your plea for mercy before him: 'If you will indeed remain in this land, I will build you up and not tear you down, and I will plant you and not uproot you; for I have relented of the evil that I said I would do to you.
[?] Do not be afraid before the king of Babylon, of whom you are afraid; do not be afraid before him, said the Lord, for I am with you to deliver you and to save you from his hand.
And I will grant you mercy, and I will have mercy on you, and I will bring you back to your land.'
But if you say, 'We will not remain in this land,' and do not listen to the voice of the Lord our God, and you say, 'No,
but we will go into the land of Egypt, and we will no longer see war, and we will not hear the sound of the trumpet, and we will not hunger for bread, and there we will settle,'
then hear the words of the Lord, you remnant of Judea. Thus says the Lord: 'If you turn your faces toward Egypt and go in to settle there,
then the sword that you fear will find you there in Egypt, and the famine, which you have spoken of fleeing from, will overtake you in Egypt, and there you will perish.

And all the men who have set their faces to go into Egypt and settle there shall perish by the sword, by famine, and by death; and none of them shall remain who escapes from the evils that I will bring upon them.'

For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: 'As my wrath and my anger were poured out upon the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so my anger will be poured out upon you who go into Egypt; and you will become a trackless waste, an object of contempt, a curse, and a reproach, and you will never see this place again.'
Thus has the Lord spoken concerning the remnant of Judah: 'Do not go into Egypt.' Now know for certain that I testify against you today

that you have done evil against yourselves, and you will regret it. For you sent me to the Lord our God and said, 'Pray for us to the Lord our God, and whatever the Lord God says to you, tell us so, and we will do it.' And I have told you,
and you have not obeyed the voice of the Lord your God in any of the words for which he sent me to you.
And now know that you will perish by the sword, by famine and by death in the place where you intend to go and settle.
And when Jeremiah had finished speaking to all the people all the words of the Lord their God, which the Lord had sent; their God [had sent him to them] with all these words,

Azariah son of Joses, Johanan son of Kareah and all the arrogant men who had said to Jeremiah, "Pray to the Lord for us," spoke. They answered Jeremiah and said to him: "You are telling a lie. The Lord our God did not send you to us, and he did not tell you, 'Do not go into Egypt to live there.'
Instead Baruch son of Neriah is turning you against us, so that you will hand us over to the Chaldeans, to kill us and destroy us in Babylon."
And Johanan son of Kareah, all the commanders of the forces and all the people did not obey the voice of the Lord to live in the land of Judah.

And Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces carried off as captives the whole remnant of Judah who had returned from all the nations where they had been scattered, to live in the land of Judah:

fathers and mothers, children, the people and the king's daughters, and the people whom Nebuzaradan the matakaran [?] had left with Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, as well as Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch [?] son of Neriah.
And they went into Egypt, because they did not listen to the voice of the Lord, and they came as far as Tahpanhes.
And the word of the Lord came to Jeremiah in Tahpanhes, and it said:
"Take large stones and hide them in a hiding place in the brickwork in front of the doors of Pharaoh's house, while the sons of Judah watch.

And say to them: 'Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will send for and bring Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, my servant. He will set up his throne on these stones that you have hidden, and he will lay his equipment on them, and he will take the equipment from them.

And he will come and strike the land of Egypt: those meant for death to death, those meant for captivity to captivity, and those meant for the sword to the sword. And he will set fire to the houses of the gods of the Egyptians.
And he will burn them and carry them off as captives. He will pick the land of Egypt clean, as a shepherd picks the lice from his garment, and he will go away in peace.
And he will smash the pillars of the City of the Sun that are in On, and he will burn the houses of their gods with fire.'"
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord about all the Jews who had settled in Egypt and who lived in Tahpanhes, Migdol, Memphis and the land of Pathros. It said:
"Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: You have seen all the evil that I brought on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah. Behold, today they lie desolate, without inhabitants,
because of the wickedness with which they provoked me to bitterness. They went to burn incense to foreign gods and to serve them, gods whom neither they nor their fathers knew.
And I sent to you my servants the prophets, sending them early and often, and I told you, 'Do not do this abominable thing, which I hate.'
But they did not listen to me, and they did not pay attention. They did not turn from their wickedness and stop burning incense to foreign gods.
And my wrath and my anger were poured out, and a fire was kindled in the gates of Judah and around Jerusalem; and they became a desolation and a trackless waste, as it is to this day.

And thus said the Lord Sabaoth, the God of Israel: Why are you doing great evils against your own souls, destroying your fathers and your mothers, infants and sucklings, from the midst of Judah, so that not one of you will be left,

provoking me with the works of your hands, burning incense to foreign gods in the land of Egypt, where you have gone to sojourn, so that you will be cut off and become a curse and a reproach among all the nations of the earth?
Have you forgotten the evil of your fathers, and your own evils, and the evils of the kings of Judah, and the evils of your wives, which they did in the land of Judah and around Jerusalem?

And they have not ceased to this very day, and they have not feared, nor have they kept to my law, nor have they followed in the path of my commandments, which I set before the face of their fathers and before their face.
Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will set my face against you for evil,

to wipe out all Judah. And they shall carry away all the remnant of Judah who resolved to go into the land of Egypt to sojourn there, so that the remnant of Judah who are in Egypt may perish and fall by the sword and by famine, and be brought to an end from the least to the greatest. By sword and by famine they shall be destroyed, and let them become a byword in oaths, a thing destroyed, a curse and a reproach.
And I will bring punishment on those who live in Egypt, as I brought punishment on Jerusalem, by sword, by famine and by death.

And none of them shall escape, nor shall anyone of the remnant of Judah who came to sojourn in the land of Egypt survive, so as to return to the land of Judah, to which they [?] in their souls to return there, except fugitives.

And all the men who knew that their wives burned incense to foreign gods answered Jeremiah, and so did all the women who stood there, a great assembly, and all the people who lived in the land of Egypt, in the land of Pathros, and they said:
As for the word that you spoke to us in the name of the Lord, we will not listen to you,

but we will certainly do every word that has gone out of our mouth: to burn incense to the queen of heaven and to offer sacrifices to her, as we did, we and our fathers, and our rulers and our kings, in the cities of Judah and in the surroundings of Jerusalem. Then we had our fill of bread, and we were well off, and we saw no evil.
But since we stopped burning incense to the queen of heaven and offering sacrifices to her, we have all been in want, and we have been wasting away by sword and by famine.
And the women said: When we burned incense to the queen of heaven and offered sacrifices to her, was it without our husbands that we made her fragrant [cakes?] and laid out offerings [?] for her?
And Jeremiah spoke to all the people, to the men of rank, to the women, and to all the people who had given him this answer, and he said:

Was it not the incense that you burned in the cities of Judah and in the streets of Jerusalem, you and your fathers, your kings and your rulers and the people of the land, that the Lord remembered and considered in his heart?

And the Lord could no longer bear it, because of the wickedness of your ways and because of the abominations that you committed. So your land became desolate and without roads, and a curse, with no one living in it, as it is this day,

because of those to whom you burned incense, and because you sinned against the Lord, did not listen to the voice of the Lord, and did not walk in his law, his testimonies and his commandments. And evil has found you, as it is this day.
And Jeremiah said to all the people and to the women: Hear the word of the Lord, all you Judeans who are in the land of Egypt.

Thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: You and your wives have spoken with your mouths and done it with your hands, and you said, 'We will surely carry out the vows we made, to burn incense to the queen of heaven and to offer sacrifices to her.' And you held fast to your vows, and you have indeed carried out your vows.

Therefore hear the word of the Lord, all you Judeans who dwell in the land of Egypt: Behold, I have sworn by my great name, said the Lord God, that my name shall no longer be spoken by the mouth of any Judean, saying, 'The Lord God lives,' in all the land of Egypt.
For behold, I have kept watch over them for their harm and not for their good, and all Judah who have settled in the land of Egypt shall perish by the sword and by famine until they are gone.

And those who escape the sword shall return from the land of Egypt to the land of Judah, few in number. And all the remnant of Judah who are sojourning in the land of Egypt shall understand whose [?] word will stand, mine or theirs.
And this shall be a sign to you, said the Lord, that I will punish you in this place with evil, so that you may know that my words against you for evil will surely be fulfilled.

Thus said the Lord: Behold, I will give Pharaoh the king into the hands of his enemies and into the hands of those who seek his life, just as I gave the king of Judah into the hands of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, his enemy, who sought his life.
The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah, when he wrote these words in a book at Jeremiah's dictation, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
Thus said the Lord, the God of Israel, concerning you, Baruch:
Because you said, 'Woe is me, woe is me, for the Lord has added toil to my pain; I lay down groaning and found no rest.'
Thus said the Lord: Say this to him: Behold, what I have built I will tear down, and what I have planted I will also uproot, together with the whole land.

And you are seeking great things for yourself? Do not seek them. For behold, I will bring evil on all flesh, says the Lord, but I will give you your life as a prize of war in every place where you go.
What Jeremiah prophesied concerning the nations of Elam.
Thus says the Lord: The bow of Elam shall be broken, the source of all their strength.
And I will send against Elam four winds from the four ends of heaven, and I will scatter them to all the winds, and there will be no nation to which the scattered people of Elam do not come.
And I will make them tremble before their enemies who seek their lives, and I will send upon them the wrath of my anger, and I will send my sword after them until I have destroyed them.
And I will set my throne in Elam, and I will destroy from it the king and its rich men.
And it shall be in the last days that I will bring back the captivity of Elam, said the Lord.
At the beginning of the reign of King Zedekiah this word came concerning Elam.

The word that came from the Lord to Jeremiah the prophet concerning all the nations; concerning Egypt, against the [?] (army?) of Pharaoh Necho, king of Egypt, which was by the river Euphrates at Carchemish, which Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, struck down in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
Take up armour and shield, and come out to battle;
saddle your horses; mount, you horsemen; put on your coats of mail and set on your helmets; bring out your spears.
Why do these tremble and flee backward? For their mighty men shall be destroyed. They fled headlong and did not turn back, surrounded on every side, said the Lord.
Let not the swift flee, and let not the mighty escape; in the north, by the Euphrates, they have grown weak and fallen.
Who is this who rises up like a river, and whose waters surge like rivers?
Egypt rises like a river, and its waves are stirred up like rivers, and it said: I will go up and cover the earth, and I will destroy the city and its inhabitants.
Mount the horses, make ready the chariots; come out, you warriors, Ethiopians, and armed Libyans, and Lydians; go up, bend the bow.

And that day is the day of the Lord our God, a day of vengeance, to take vengeance on his enemies. The sword shall devour and be sated and be drunk with their blood, for it is a sacrifice of the Lord Sabaoth in the land of the north by the river Euphrates.
Go up to Gilead and take balm for the virgin daughter of Egypt; in vain have you multiplied your remedies; there is no benefit for you.
The nations have heard your voice, and the earth is filled with your crying, for warrior has grown weak against warrior; both have fallen together.
What the Lord spoke by the mouth of Jeremiah the prophet concerning the coming of Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, to strike down the land of Egypt.
Declare it in Egypt and make it heard in Migdol, and announce it in Memphis and Tahpanhes. Say: Rise up and make yourself ready, for the sword has devoured your [?].
For that chosen calf of yours has fled; it did not stand, for the Lord has undone it.
And its multitude grew weak and fell. Each man spoke to his neighbour and said: Let us rise up and return to our own people and to the land of our homeland, away from the sword of the nations.
Call the name of Pharaoh, king of Egypt, 'Saon Ebirta Moeth' [?]; the time has come.
As I live, says the Lord, the King of hosts is his name: as Tabor is among the mountains and Carmel is in the midst of the sea, so it shall come.
Make vessels of captivity for yourself, you who dwell in the daughter of Egypt, for Memphis shall be given to destruction, and it shall be called 'Woe' because it has no inhabitants.
Egypt is a beautiful heifer; stingers [?] from the north have come upon it.

And her hired soldiers in her midst were like fatted calves, for they too turned back and fled together; they did not stand, for the day of destruction had come upon them, and the time of their punishment.
Her voice is like a hissing serpent, for they marched through the sand; men with axes came against her.
Cut down her forest like woodcutters, says the Lord God, for it will no longer [?]; they are more numerous than locusts, and there is no counting them.
The daughter of Egypt has been put to shame; she has been handed over to a people from the north, said the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel.
Behold, I will bring vengeance on Amos, his son, on Pharaoh, on his gods, and on those who trust in them.
And I will hand them over to those who seek their lives, to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and to his servants. After this they will dwell as in the former days, said the Lord.

But you, do not be afraid, my servant Jacob, and do not tremble, Israel, for behold, I will save you from afar, and your descendants from the land of their captivity. Jacob will return and dwell in quiet; he will sleep, and there will no longer be anyone to oppress him.

And you, do not be afraid, my servant Jacob, said the Lord, for I am with you. I will make an end of all the nations to which I have sent you, but I will not make an end of you. I will discipline you with judgment, and I will by no means leave you unpunished.
Concerning the Philistines: the word of the Lord that came to the prophet Jeremiah concerning the slaughter of the Philistines, before Pharaoh of Gaza [?].

Thus says the Lord: Behold, waters will rise out of the north and become an overflowing torrent. They will flood the land and everything in it, the city and those who live in it. People will cry out, and all the inhabitants of the land will wail
at the sound of his advance, at his mighty weapons, at the rumbling of chariots and the noise of his wheels. Fathers will not turn back for their children, because their hands have gone limp.

On the day that is coming to destroy all the Philistines, I will destroy Tyre and Sidon and all the rest of their helpers, for the Lord will wipe out the Philistines who remain in the islands, and Cappadocia.
Baldness has come upon Gaza; Ashkelon has been cast down [?]; and the remnant that is in Akim, how long will you gather together?
How long will you keep cutting, O sword of the Lord? How long will you not rest? Go back into your sheath.
Rest and be still. And the Lord has given it orders against Ashkelon and against those who live on the seacoast, to rise up against the remnant.

Concerning Moab. Thus said the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Woe to Nebo, for it has perished! Kiriathaim has been captured and carried off; the stronghold of Moab has been put to shame, and they have been defeated.
There is no more joy in Heshbon of Moab; they have plotted evil against her: 'Come, let us cut her off from among the nations.' And Madmen will be utterly silenced; the sword will pursue you,
for there is the sound of people crying out from Horonaim, with ruin and great destruction:
'Moab is shattered.' Announce it to Zoar and to her young men,
for Luhith is filled with weeping, for they went up the stony ascent weeping bitterly, for the enemies were on the descent of Horonaim. The anguish and the cry of destruction were heard.
Flee and save yourselves, and become like wild asses in the desert.
For because you trusted in your strongholds, troubles will come upon you and seize you, and Chemosh will go out into captivity, and his priests and his princes together.
And destruction will come upon every city, and no city will escape; the valleys will perish and the plains will be laid waste, as the Lord has said.
Give a sign to Moab, for she will be utterly forsaken; and all her cities will become desolate, without a road, because there are no inhabitants in them.
Cursed be anyone who does the work of the Lord carelessly, and cursed be anyone who keeps his sword back from blood.

Moab has been at ease since his youth, and trusted in his glory; he has not been poured from vessel to vessel, and he has not gone into captivity. Therefore his taste has remained in him, and his scent has not faded.
Therefore, behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when I will send against him men who tip vessels, and they will tip him over; they will crush his vessels, and his horns will be broken.
And Moab will be ashamed of Chemosh, as the house of Israel was ashamed of Bethel, their hope.
How can you say, 'We are strong, and men mighty in battle'?
Moab has perished, and her cities, and her chosen young men have gone down to the slaughter, says the King; the Lord of hosts is his name.
The day of Moab is near at hand, and his calamity comes very swiftly.
Lament for him, all you who are around him, all you who know his name; say to him: How the staff of glory has been broken, and the rod of wealth!
Come down from your glory and sit on the damp ground, daughter of Dibon, for Moab has perished; the destroyer of your strongholds has come up against you.
Stand by the road and watch, you who live in Aroer, and ask the one who flees and the one who has escaped, and say: What has happened?
Moab is put to shame, for he is broken; wail and cry out; tell it at the Arnon that Moab has perished.
And judgment comes upon the land of Mishor, upon Holon, and upon Jahzah and Mephaath,
and upon Dibon, and upon Nebo, and upon Beth-diblathaim,
and upon Kiriathaim, and upon Beth-gamul, and upon Beth-meon,
and upon Kerioth, and upon Bozrah, and upon all the cities of the land of Moab, far and near.
The horn of Moab is cut off, and his arrogance is broken, says the Lord.
Make him drunk, for he spoke proudly against the Lord; and Moab will strike with his own hand, and he himself will become a laughingstock,
just as Israel was a laughingstock to you. Or was he found stealing from you, that you fought against him? Now you flee to him.
The inhabitants of Moab have left their cities and settled on the rock; they have become like doves nesting in the rock at the mouth of the caves.
I have heard of Moab's insolence, for he has insulted me greatly; I have seen his wantonness, his insolence and his arrogance, and his heart was lifted up.
But I know his deeds, says the Lord. Was it not enough for him? His arms did not do as much as that. [?]
Therefore wail over Moab, over Moab on every side; cry out over the men of the wall, the shaven-headed, and a voice will be raised,

as with the weeping of Jazer they will weep for you, O vine of Sibmah. Your branches have crossed over to the sea, O city of Jazer. It has come upon your fruit and upon your harvest, and destruction has fallen upon your grape-gatherers [?].
Gladness and joy have been snatched away from the land of the Moabites. There was wine in your winepresses, but they did not tread it, neither in the morning nor in the evening.

And the cry of Heshbon reached as far as Elealeh, and as far as Jahaz they raised their voice. Their cities raised their voice from Zoar to Horonaim, Eglath-shelishiyah, for it is a heifer [?] [?], for the waters of Nimrim will also be burned up [?].
And I will destroy from Moab, says the Lord, the one who goes up to the high place and the one who burns incense to their idols.
Therefore the heart of Moab will moan like a pipe. My heart will moan like a pipe over the men by the wall who shave their hair, because of this: what he had saved has perished from among men.
All heads in every place will be shaved, and all beards will be shaved, and all hands will beat the breast, and there will be sackcloth on all loins.
And on all the roofs of Moab and in all its streets there will be mourning, for I have broken Moab like a vessel that is no longer of any use, says the Lord.
How it has been defeated! Wail. How Moab has turned its back! Moab was put to shame and became a thing of reproach and a terror to all those around it,
for thus says the Lord: Behold, he will swoop down like an eagle, and spread his wings over Moab.
And Kerioth has been taken and its strongholds seized, and in that day the heart of the mighty men of Moab will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
And Moab will perish from among its multitude, for it spoke arrogantly against the Lord.
Fear and the pit and the snare are upon you who dwell in Moab, says the Lord.

Whoever flees from the face of fear will fall into the pit, and whoever climbs up out of the pit will be caught in the snare, for I will bring this upon Moab in the year when I visit them, says the Lord.
Those who fled from the snare stood in the shelter of Heshbon, for fire came out of Heshbon and a flame from the city of Sihon, and it devoured the leaders of Moab and roused [?] the sons of Sihon.
Woe to you, Moab! You have perished, people of Chemosh, for they will carry off your sons as plunder and your daughters into captivity.
And I will bring back the captives of Moab in the last days, says the Lord. Here ends the judgment on Moab.
Concerning the sons of Ammon. Thus says the Lord: Has Israel no children? Or has he no heir? Why then has Milcom taken possession of Gilead, and his people settled in its cities?

Therefore, behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will make the clamor of war heard against Rabbah of the sons of Ammon. It will become a ruin [?] and a thing for destruction, its high places will be burned with fire, and Israel will take possession of its own dominion, says the Lord.

Wail, Heshbon, for the strength of Ai [?] has perished. Cry out, daughters of Rabbah, put on sackcloth and lament, and run about on the walls, for Milcom will go into captivity, his priests and his princes together.
Why do you rejoice in the valleys of the Anakim? Your valleys have flowed away [?], O shameless daughter, you who trust in your treasures and say, “Who will come against me?”

Behold, I will bring terror upon you, says the Lord of hosts, from all those who live around you. Each of you will be scattered straight ahead, and there will be no one to gather those who are scattered.
And after this I will bring back the captives of the sons of Ammon, says the Lord.
Concerning Edom. Thus says the Lord of hosts: There is no more wisdom in Teman. Counsel has perished from the prudent; their wisdom has gone.
And go down deep to dwell, you inhabitants of Dedan, for it has become hard [?]. I will bring [disaster] upon him at the time when I visit him.
For grape-gatherers will come upon you who will not leave you any gleanings. Like thieves in the night they will lay their hands on you,

for I have overthrown Esau. I will uncover their hidden places, and they will not be able to hide at all. Their offspring has perished by the hand of his brother and of his neighbor, and he is no more.
The one who spoke of leaving your orphans [?], so that they might be saved: I will save them, and your widows will put their hope in me.
For thus says the Lord: Behold, those who were not meant to drink the cup have drunk it, and will you be acquitted? You will not be acquitted,
for I have sworn by myself, says the Lord, that she will be a desolation, a reproach, and a curse in her midst, and all her cities will be desolate forever.
I have heard a report from the Lord, and he has sent messengers to the nations: "Gather together and come against her, and rise up to fight against her."
Behold, small indeed [?], and I have made you contemptible to the nations among men.

Your insolence has brought this upon you; the shamelessness of your heart made you dwell in the clefts of the rocks. You seized the strongholds of the high hills, for you raised your nest high like an eagle, and from there I will cast you down, says the Lord.
And Edom will be a desolation. Everyone who passes by will be astonished and will hiss at all her wounds.
Just as Sodom and Gomorrah and their neighbors were overthrown, says the Lord Almighty, no one will live there any longer, and no son of man will settle there.

Behold, like a lion he will come up from the Jordan to the place of Etham, for I will quickly drive them out of it and set young men over it. And who is chosen against him? I will visit [it], for who is like me, and who will stand against me, and who is the shepherd who will stand before my face?

Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord which he has planned against Edom, and the purpose which he has formed against the inhabitants of Teman: surely the remnants of their sheep will be dragged away [?], surely their dwelling will be made desolate over them.
At the sound of their fall the earth shook; your cry in the Red Sea, your voice, was heard.
Behold, like an eagle he will come up and rustle [?], and spread his wings over her strongholds. On that day the heart of the mighty men of Edom will be like the heart of a woman in labor.
Concerning Damascus. Hamath and Arpad are put to shame, for they have heard bad news. They have lost heart in the sea and are in turmoil; they cannot find rest.
Damascus has grown weak. She turned to flee and rushed away; trembling seized her, and pain seized her like a woman giving birth.
How has he not left my city, my beloved one? He loved the praiseworthy land [?].
Therefore your young men shall fall in your streets, and all your fathers, the warriors, shall fall on that day, said the Lord of hosts.
And I will kindle a fire in the walls of Damascus, and it shall devour the lanes of the son of Ader.
Concerning Kedar, the queen of the court, which Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, struck down. Thus said the Lord: Arise and go up to Kedar, and destroy the sons of Kedem.
Their tents and their flocks they shall carry off; their garments and their camels and all their vessels they shall carry off for themselves. Proclaim against them destruction from round about.

Flee quickly, and scatter, and go deep into hiding, you who dwell in the court, said the Lord, for Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, has devised a plan against you and has conceived a purpose against you.
Arise and go up against the nation that is at ease, which dwells in rest, said the Lord, which has no doors and no bolts; they dwell alone.

And their camels shall become spoil, and the multitude of their flocks shall be for destruction; and I will scatter them to every wind, those who have shaved their faces, and from every nation I will bring about their rout, said the Lord.
And that court shall become a dwelling place for ostriches, and it shall be without a road forever. No man shall dwell there, nor shall any son of man settle there.
The word which the Lord spoke concerning Babylon, the land of the Chaldeans, by the hand of Jeremiah the prophet.

Declare it among the nations, and make it heard, and raise a standard; proclaim it, do not hide it; say: Babylon has been laid waste; Bel the fearless has been put to shame. The pampered Merodach has been given up; her carved images have been put to shame.
For a nation has come up against her from the north; it shall make her land a ruin, and there shall be no inhabitant in it, from man to beast. They have been shaken and have departed.
In those days, said the Lord, and at that time the sons of Israel shall come, they and the sons of Judah together; they shall go weeping, and they shall go and seek the Lord their God.
For they shall turn their faces hither, and they shall come and take refuge in the Lord, for the everlasting covenant shall not be forgotten.
Like lost sheep, so my people has become; their shepherds scattered them on the mountains; they led them astray; they went from the mountains onto the hills; they forgot their resting place.
All who found them devoured them. Their enemies said: Let us not spare them, because they sinned against the Lord, the law of righteousness, the Lord who gathered their fathers.
Separate yourselves from Babylon, and come out of the land of the Chaldeans, and be like dragons before the sheep.

For behold, I will raise up and bring against Babylon assemblies of great nations from the land of the north, and they shall array themselves against her, and by her they shall be destroyed. Their arrows are like the arrow of a skilled warrior; it shall not return empty.
And Chaldea shall become plunder; all who plunder her shall be sated, said the Lord.
For you rejoiced and boasted in seizing my inheritance, and because you frisked like heifers in the green grass, and butted like bulls,
your mother has been greatly put to shame; the mother who bore you was buried [?] well; and behold, the last of the nations: desolate, waterless and without a road.
Because of the wrath of the Lord it shall not be inhabited, and it shall become a desolation. Everyone who passes through Babylon shall be dismayed, and shall hiss at all her wounds.
Draw up in battle array against Babylon, all around her, all you who bend the bow. Shoot at her; do not spare your arrows, for she has sinned against the Lord.

Overpower her on every side. Her hands have been loosed, her battlements have fallen, and her wall has been torn down. For vengeance comes from the Lord: take vengeance on her. Do to her as she has done.
Wipe out the seed of Babylon, and the one who holds the sickle at harvest time, before the sword of the nations. Each man shall turn back to his own people, and each man shall flee to his own land.
Israel is a straying sheep; lions have scattered him. First the king of Assyria devoured him, and after that Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, devoured his bones.
Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: Behold, I will take vengeance on the king of Babylon and on his land, as I took vengeance on the king of Assyria.
And I will bring Israel back to his pasture, and he shall graze on Carmel and in Bashan, on Mount Ephraim and in the land of Gilead, and their souls shall be satisfied.

In those days and at that time, says the Lord, they shall look for the iniquity of Israel, and there shall be none, and for the sins of Judah, and they shall not find them, for I will be merciful to their remnant on the earth, says the Lord.

Come up bitterly against the land of those who embitter, and take vengeance on its inhabitants, O sword, and destroy, for after them comes evil, says the Lord. And do everything that I have commanded you.
The sound of battle, and great destruction in the land of the Chaldeans,
how the hammer of the whole earth has been broken and shattered, how Babylon has become a desolation among the nations.
Prophecy of Jeremiah. I will fight against you, and they shall come against you [?] and seize you, Babylon, and you did not know it. You were found and taken, because you opposed the Lord.
The Lord has opened his treasury and brought out the weapons of his wrath, for this is the work of the Lord God of hosts in the land of the Chaldeans.
For her times have come. Open her storehouses; search her out like a cave; wipe her out; let nothing of her remain.
Dry up all her fruit, and let them go down to the slaughter. Woe to them, for their day has come, and the time of their punishment.
The voice of those who flee and escape from the land of the Babylonians, to declare in Zion the vengeance of the Lord our God, the vengeance for his temple.

Summon many against Babylon, every one who bends the bow. Besiege her all around; let none of her escape. Repay her according to her deeds; do to her all that she has done, for she opposed the Lord, the Holy God of Israel.
Therefore her young men shall fall in her streets, and all her fathers [?], her warriors, shall be cast down on that day, says the Lord.
Behold, I am against you, O insolent one, says the Lord of hosts. For the day of your fall is coming, and the time of your punishment.
And your insolence shall grow weak and fall, and there shall be no one to raise it up. And I will kindle fire in her forests, and it shall devour everything around her.
Thus says the Lord of hosts: The sons of Israel and the sons of Judah are oppressed together. All who took them captive oppress them, and they refused to let them go.
But their Redeemer is strong; the Lord Almighty is his name. He will bring judgment against his enemies, so that the land may be destroyed, and he will be angry with the inhabitants of Babylon.
A sword upon the Chaldeans, says the Lord, and upon the inhabitants of Babylon and upon her rich men;
a sword upon her sorceries, and they will be destroyed; a sword upon her warriors, and they will grow weak; a sword upon her horses and upon her chariots;
a sword upon her warriors and upon the mixed people in her midst, and they will become like women; a sword upon her treasures, and they will be plundered;
a sword upon her waters, in which she trusted, and they dried up.

And they were put to shame by their carved images and by their groves, in which she boasted. Therefore dragons will dwell in the groves, and the daughters of ostriches will dwell there. It will never again be built, and no one will live in it from generation to generation.
As God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah and the land around them, says the Lord, no one will live there, and no son of man will stay there.
Behold, a people is coming from the north, and a great nation and many kings will rise from the ends of the earth.
Archers and spearmen, they are merciless, and they will show no pity. Their voice will roar like the sea. They ride on horses, ready like fire for battle against you, O daughter of Babylon.
The king of Babylon heard the report about them, and his hands went limp. Distress seized him, pangs like those of a woman giving birth.

Behold, like a lion he will come up from the thickets of the Jordan to the place of Etham, against the ancient dwelling place. For I will quickly drive them out of it, and I will set all the young men over it. For who is like me, and who will stand against me, and who is the shepherd who can stand before my face?

Therefore hear the counsel of the Lord, which he has planned against Babylon, and the purpose he has formed against the inhabitants of Chaldea: until the lambs of their flocks are destroyed, until their pasture is laid waste by them.
For at the sound of Babylon's destruction the earth will shake, and her cry will be heard among the nations.
Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will stir up against Babylon and against the inhabitants of Chaldea the heart of those who rise up in haste [?], a burning and destroying wind.
And I will send scorners against Babylon, and they will scorn her and lay waste her land. For woe will be upon Babylon all around in the day of her affliction.
Let the archer bend his bow against her, and let whoever has armour put it on against her. Do not spare her young men; destroy all her strength.
And the wounded will fall in the land of the Chaldeans, and those who were run through will fall outside.
For Israel and Judah have not been widowed of their God, the Lord Almighty, though their land was filled with lawlessness against the holy ones of Israel.
Flee from Babylon, and let each of you save his own life. Do not be caught up in their iniquities, for it is the time of the Lord's vengeance, and he will repay her what she deserves.
Babylon is a golden cup in the hands of the Lord, making all the earth drunk. The nations drank of her wine, and because of it the nations were stirred up.
And suddenly Babylon has fallen and been shattered. Lament over her, and take healing balm for her wound, in case she might somehow be healed.

We tried to heal Babylon, but she was not healed. Let us leave her and go away, each to his own land, for her judgment has reached to heaven; her sentence has risen as high as the heavens and has reached up to the stars.
And the Lord has brought forth his judgment. Come, and let us tell in Zion the works of the Lord our God.

Make the arrows ready; fill your quivers. The Lord has stirred up the spirit of the king of the [?] (Medes?), for his wrath is upon Babylon to destroy her. It is the Lord's vengeance, the vengeance for his temple.
Raise a standard against Babylon; post watchmen; set up men in ambush; make ready the weapons. For the Lord has begun, and he will do all that he has spoken against the inhabitants of Babylon.
You who dwell upon many waters and upon your many treasures, your end has come, truly, into the courts of your heart.
For the Lord has sworn by his arm: “I will fill you with troops as with locusts, and they will shout over you like those who tread the winepress.”
It is he who made the earth by his power, prepared the world by his wisdom, and by his understanding stretched out the heaven;
at the sound of his thunder he placed a multitude of waters in heaven; he brought up clouds from the end of the earth, made lightnings for the rain, and brought out light from his treasuries.
Every man has become foolish in his knowledge; every goldsmith is put to shame by his carved images, for he has breathed falsehood into them; there is no breath in them.
The things they have made are worthless, objects of mockery; at the time of their visitation they will perish.
The portion of Jacob is not like these, for he who created all things is himself his portion, and Israel is the rod of his inheritance. The Lord of hosts is his name.
You scatter the weapons of war for me, and through you I will scatter nations, and through you I will destroy kings.
Through you I will scatter horses and their riders,

and through you I will scatter chariots and those who ride in them. Through you I will scatter man and woman; through you I will scatter old man and youth; through you I will scatter young man and maiden.
Through you I will scatter the shepherd and his flock; through you I will scatter the farmers and their produce; and through you I will scatter your rulers and your leaders.
And I will repay Babylon and the inhabitants of Chaldea for all the evil they did in Zion before your eyes, says the Lord.

Behold, I am against you, O corrupt mountain, says the Lord, you destroyer of all the earth. I will stretch out my hand against you, roll you down from the rocks, and make you like a burnt-out mountain.
No one will take from you a stone for a corner or a stone for a foundation, for you will be a ruin forever, the Lord has said.

Raise a standard in the land; blow the trumpet among the nations; consecrate the tribes against her. Summon against her, on my behalf, the kings of Ararat and the Ashkenazites. Set up [?] (siege engines?) against her; bring up horses against her like a multitude of locusts.
Consecrate the nations against her: the king of the Medes [?] and his rulers, and all his leaders from every land of his dominion.
The earth shook and was in pain, because the Lord's plan has awakened against Babylon, to make the land of Babylon a desolation, so that no one will live there any longer.
The warriors of Babylon have stopped fighting. They sat besieged, their strength was broken, and they became like women. Her dwellings were set on fire, and her bars were broken.
One runner runs to meet another, and the [?] meets the one who raises the cry, to tell the king of Babylon that his city has perished.
From the far end of her outlets they have been seized, and their fullness [?] they have burned with fire, and her men of war have gone out from her.
For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: The houses of the king of Babylon will be threshed like threshing floors in summer. In a little while her threshing will come.

Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, has torn me apart and devoured me, and has come upon me like a little darkness [?]. He has set me down like a worthless vessel. He has swallowed me like a dragon and filled his belly with my delights.
He has taken my labours far from me [?]. “Let my miseries be upon Babylon,” the inhabitant of Zion will say. “And let my blood be upon the inhabitants of Chaldea,” Israel will say.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will judge your adversary and take vengeance for you. I will lay waste her wall and dry up her waters.
And Babylon will become a desolation and a dwelling place for dragons, heaps of ruins and an object of hissing, and no one will live there any longer.
Together [?] her young men have risen up like lions, and like lions' cubs.
In their heat I will give them their drink and make them drunk, so that they grow faint [?], and sleep an everlasting sleep, and never wake again, says the Lord.
And I will bring them down like lambs to the slaughter, and like rams together with kids.
How Sheshach has perished, and the pride of the whole earth has been captured! How Babylon has become a desolation among all the nations!
The sea has risen over Babylon with the roar of its waves and has covered her.
Her cities have become a desolate land, a waterless and pathless land, where no man will live, and no son of man will stay.
And I will take vengeance on Bel in Babylon, and I will take from his mouth what he has swallowed. The nations will no longer gather to him, and the wall of Babylon will fall.
Come out of her, my people, and let each one of you save himself from the anger of the Lord.

Do not let your hearts ever tremble, and do not be afraid of the report that is heard in that land. The report will come in one year, and after it, in the next year, another report, and lawlessness in the land, and dominion upon dominion, proverb upon proverb.
Therefore, behold, the days are coming when I will bring punishment on all the carved images of Babylon. Her whole land will be put to shame, and all her wounded will fall in her midst.
And heaven and earth and all that is in them will rejoice over Babylon, for her destroyers will come from the north, said the Lord.
And in Babylon all the wounded from the whole earth will fall.
You who have escaped from his land, go on and do not stand still. Remember the Lord from far away, and call Jerusalem to mind in your hearts.
You were put to shame, for you heard our reproach. Disgrace covered our face; foreigners entered our holy places, the house of the Lord.
Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, when I will take vengeance on her carved images, and throughout all her land her wounded shall fall.
Even if Babylon should rise up like the heavens, and even if she makes the height of her strength impossible to reach, her destroyers shall come from me, says the Lord.
A sound of crying out in Babylon, and great destruction in the land of the Chaldeans,
for the Lord has wiped out Babylon and destroyed from her the great sound of groaning, like many waters; he has given her voice over to destruction.
For misery has come upon Babylon; her wise men have been slain, and their bows have become feeble, for God is one who repays.

The Lord himself will repay her what she deserves. Her warriors and her judges, her prophets and her mighty men shall be made drunk with drunkenness, and they shall sleep an eternal sleep and never wake again, says the Lord. The Ruler of [?] is his name.

Thus says the Lord of hosts: I will destroy the wall of Babylon. Tear it down, and let it be torn down, and let her gates be burned with fire. The peoples shall toil in vain, and the nations shall fail from the very start.

The word that Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Manasseh, to speak when he went from Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon, in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was the chief of gifts.
Jeremiah wrote all this evil that was to come upon Babylon in one book, together with all these words that are written about Babylon.
And Jeremiah said to Seraiah: When you come to Babylon and see it, read aloud all these words,
and say: 'O Lord, you have spoken against this place for its destruction, so that there will be no inhabitant in it, from man to beast, for its ruin shall last forever.'
And when you have finished reading this book, tie a stone to it and throw it into the middle of the Euphrates,
and say: 'Thus shall Babylon sink, and it shall not rise again because of the evils that have been sent upon it.' Here end the words of Jeremiah.
Zedekiah was twenty-one years old when he became king, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem. His mother's name was Hamutal, the daughter of Jeremiah, from Libnah.
He did evil in the sight of the Lord, as Jehoiakim had done.
For the anger of the Lord was against Jerusalem and Judah until he cast them out from his presence. And Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.

In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and all his army came against Jerusalem, and they built a siege wall of hewn stone all around it.
And the city was under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
In the fourth month, on the ninth day of the month, the famine grew severe in the city, and there was no more bread for the people of the land.

And the city could no longer hold out, and all the fighting men fled. The king and all his people left the city by night, by way of the gate between the wall and the outer wall, which was near the royal garden. The Chaldeans were all around the city.
And they went by the road to Arabia, and the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king,

and they overtook King Zedekiah beyond Jericho, in the wilderness, and all his servants were scattered. They seized King Zedekiah and brought him to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and King Nebuchadnezzar passed judgment on Zedekiah.
And the king of Babylon killed Zedekiah's sons before his eyes, and he killed all the princes of Judah at Riblah.
And he put out Zedekiah's eyes and bound him in fetters. The king of Babylon brought him to Babylon and put him in the mill-house until the day of his death.
And in the fifth month, on the tenth day of the month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard, who served the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.
And he burned the temple of the Lord and the king's house. He burned all the houses of the city and all the great houses with fire.
And the army of the Chaldeans that was with the chief of the guard tore down all the wall around Jerusalem.

But Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard carried away into captivity the lowly of the people, and the rest of the people who were left in the city, and the deserters who had gone over to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the people.
But Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard left the poor of the land to be vinedressers.

And the Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars that were in the house of the Lord, and the stands, and the bronze sea that was in the house of the Lord, and they carried all the bronze away to Babylon.
And they took away the [?], the lifting tools, the rims [?], the [?], the bowls [?], the [?], and all the bronze vessels used in the temple service, and the censers and the [?],
and the [?], the snuffers, the strainers, the lampstands, the [?], and the cups. The chief of the guard took away everything that was made of gold and of silver.
As for the two pillars, the one sea, and the twelve bronze calves under the sea, which King Solomon had made in the house of the Lord, the bronze of all these vessels could not be weighed.
As for the pillars, each pillar was thirty-five cubits high, and a cord of twelve cubits reached all the way around it. Its thickness all around was four [fingers?],

and on them were bronze capitals. Each capital was five cubits high, and there was a network with pomegranates all around the capital, all of bronze. The second pillar was made the same way, with eight pomegranates to each cubit over the ten cubits.
There were ninety-six pomegranates on one side only, and in all there were a hundred pomegranates on the network all around.
And the chief of the guard took away Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three doorkeepers.

And from the city he took one eunuch, who was in charge of the men of war, and seven men of renown who served before the king, who were found in the city; and the scribe, the chief of the forces, who enrolled all the people of the land; and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in that city.
And Nebuzaradan the captain [?] took them away and brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
And he struck them, and the king of Babylon put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. And Judah was carried away captive from its own land.
And these are the people whom King Nebuchadnezzar carried away captive in the seventh year: of the Jews, three thousand and twenty-three.
And in the eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar he carried away captive from Jerusalem eight hundred and thirty-two souls.
And in the twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain [?] carried away captive of the Jews seven hundred and forty-five souls. And all the souls were four thousand six hundred.

And in the thirty-seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin, king of Judah, in the tenth month, on the twenty-fourth day of the month, Evil-merodach, king of Babylon, in the year in which he became king, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin, king of Judah, and brought him out of the prison house.
And he spoke kindly to him, and gave him a seat higher than all the seats of the kings who were with him in Babylon.
And he changed his prison garments for him, and he ate bread before him continually all his days, as long as he lived.
And he assigned him a regular allowance, and it came to him from the king of the Babylonians day by day until the day of his death, all the days of his life.
